cn_m10: A batch of 34 surplus American M10 tank destroyers was bought by the Kuomintang in 1948 and taken to Taiwan without fighting on the mainland; some were later rebuilt with Japanese 105 mm howitzers as makeshift artillery until the M7 Priest took over in the mid-1950s. In the game it matches the US M10 except that it cannot fit the add-on armour. The gun hits hard, but the turret turns very slowly, mobility is modest and the open roof leaves the crew exposed to HE and artillery, so it works best from ambush. It arrived in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_m113a1_tow: Taiwan bought 634 M113A1 carriers in the mid-1960s and later armed some Marine Corps examples with American TOW missiles on an Israeli-made RAMTA launcher; Humvees have since inherited that role. With only the missile launcher and a machine gun, it belongs well behind the front line. The missiles defeat anything without ERA or an active protection system, and the tall launcher with 20 degrees of depression can fire over even steep crests while the hull stays hidden. The catch is the launcher itself, which is exposed and fragile, and it can only swing through a narrow arc. It came with Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_m18_hellcat: The 76 mm M18 was the first combat vehicle the United States handed to the Republic of China under Korean War-era aid, arriving from 1952; 243 were delivered and they stayed in service into the 1970s, some ending up as fixed coastal guns. Speed is its main asset in the game, getting it to flanks and key positions early, where the M1 gun's APCBC shot can deal with most opponents. With thin armour and an open turret, though, almost any return fire is dangerous. It was added in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_m1a2t: Taiwan ordered 108 Abrams in 2018–2019 to replace its CM11 and M60A3 TTS fleets; the resulting M1A2T is derived from the M1A2 SEP V3 with a downgraded armour package, and at least 40 had been delivered by December 2024. It performs much like the American M1A2 SEP, suiting both aggressive and defensive play, and its strong thermal sight helps at long range and in bad weather. Like every Abrams it relies on terrain to cover a hull that even early APFSDS can defeat, and with no TUSK kit on offer, strong ATGMs are a greater threat. It arrived in Update 2.53 "Line of Contact".
cn_m24_chaffee: A handful of M24 light tanks reached Nationalist China under wartime lend-lease, and 289 more followed to Taiwan in the 1950s as Korean War-era aid, receiving various upgrades as the design aged. In the game it mixes a hard-hitting gun with good speed and passable armour, a combination best used to grab flanking positions early rather than to slug it out with enemy tanks. It has been in the Chinese tree since Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_m36: China's M36 story has two strands: the People's Volunteer Army captured one in Korea, now displayed in the Military Museum of the Chinese People's Revolution, while Taiwan's army took ten ex-French M36B2s that duelled with PLA artillery during the First Taiwan Strait Crisis and served until the late 1970s. The in-game vehicle is a copy of the American M36 GMC with one difference: it has no access to the M304 APCR shot. It arrived in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_m3a3_stuart: The M3A3 refined the Stuart with a welded, sloped hull borrowed from the M5 line and a turret bustle for the radio. Nationalist China received 48 under lend-lease to form its first tank battalion in India, and many were later captured by the PLA, which kept them until the late 1950s. Its sloped plates are the main draw in the game, turning away some small-calibre rounds that would go through the fronts of other early light tanks, though that protection is no licence to trade shots. It came with Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_m3a3_stuart_1st_ptg: This premium Stuart represents the Chinese-American 1st Provisional Tank Group, the lend-lease battalion formed in India that helped the Allies reopen the Ledo-Burma Road through Japanese-held Burma. In battle it is identical to the tech-tree M3A3, so its angled front plates give it an advantage over other early light tanks against small-calibre guns, but it is still too thinly armoured for slugging matches. It was added in the "Wind of Change" update.
cn_m41_a3_walker_bulldog: Taiwan's M41A3 was an M41A1 re-engined with a fuel-injected AOS 895-5 diesel, received from 1958 and used mainly for fire support on the outlying islands and for training until the last one retired in February 2022; 50 others were rebuilt as M41Ds. In the game it keeps the M41's excellent mobility and a gun that can defeat most WWII-era tanks when it catches them side-on, but it gives up the APDS and HEATFS rounds of other nations' versions in exchange for meeting weaker opposition. It suits careful flanking and joined the game in the "Sons of Attila" update.
cn_m42_duster: Taiwan's army and marines received the twin-40 mm M42 from 1958 to replace the M19; once supersonic jets made it outdated it was used mostly for fire support, a job it still occasionally does in exercises. The in-game version is identical to the American one. As an anti-aircraft vehicle it is considered weak, with a fully exposed crew and only 120 rounds per minute, and it lacks the armour to fight tanks openly, so survival depends on hugging cover and limiting exposure.
cn_m48a1_patton_III: Taiwan bought 309 ex-US Army M48A1s between 1973 and 1980 under Project Fire Bull to counter the PLA's Type 59s, and they formed the core of its armour until M60A3 TTS tanks arrived in the 1990s; 100 were later rebuilt with 105 mm guns as the CM12. In the game it behaves exactly like the American and Israeli M48A1. The 90 mm gun handles WWII-era tanks comfortably, but the tall, bulky hull is easy to spot and hit, so it is most useful in a supporting role. It was introduced in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_m4a1_76w_sherman: Six of these hybrid Shermans reached Taiwan's army from Britain in late 1949: they had the cast M4A1 hull and large-mantlet turret of the M4A1 (76) W but carried the older 75 mm M3 gun, and were retired in 1952 once the M18 became the main tank. Hull-down is where it shines in the game: good gun depression lets it hide the weak-spotted M4A1 hull and show only a turret better armoured than those of the Shermans it usually meets. It arrived in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_m4a4_sherman: China received 32 M4A4 Shermans through lend-lease for the 1st Provisional Tank Group in India; after the war they fought in the civil war with the New First and New Sixth Armies until defeat in the Liaoshen Campaign. The M4A4's hull was stretched by 15 cm to fit the Chrysler multibank engine, itself built from five car engines. Experienced opponents will aim for its front hull, where the hatches bulge out of the slope and the welded-on extra plates only partly make up for it. It came with Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_m4a4_sherman_1st_ptg: This premium M4A4 carries the markings of the 1st Provisional Tank Group, the lend-lease unit of the Chinese Expeditionary Forces that fought in the China-Burma-India theatre and helped reopen the Ledo-Burma Road. It is the tech-tree M4A4 with a unique camouflage and a roof-mounted M2HB, so it plays like other 75 mm Shermans, and its vertical stabiliser makes shooting on the move more practical. First sold as a pack with Update 1.91 "Night Vision", it was withdrawn after the 2021 May sale, briefly returned for China's National Day that year, and came back for Golden Eagles in the "Sky Guardians" update.
cn_m55: Six M55 self-propelled 203 mm howitzers were lent to Taiwan during the 1958 Second Taiwan Strait Crisis and posted to Kinmen, but reportedly went back to the US after just a week, partly over a friendly-fire incident, in exchange for static 8-inch guns. In the game everything rests on the howitzer, whose HE shell holds roughly 23 kg of TNT equivalent, enough to wreck any tank if placed well. With a ten-round load and a very slow reload, though, each miss is costly, and the large, thin-skinned hull rarely survives the reply. It was added in the "Tusk Force" update.
cn_m5a1_stuart: Nationalist China first got M5A1 Stuarts from the US in 1948; after heavy civil war losses, its armoured command bought tanks the Americans had left behind on Pacific islands, and one rebuilt battalion assembled 22 M5A1s from salvaged vehicles and parts. In the game it handles much like the M3A3 and other early American light tanks, built for scouting and supporting infantry rather than fighting enemy armour head-on. It arrived in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_m60a3_tts: Taiwan took 460 ex-US M60A3 TTS tanks, ordered in two batches in 1994 and 1996, to replace its ageing M48A1s, and they have served alongside the CM11 since; plans for a domestic 120 mm upgrade were dropped in favour of buying the M1A2T. In the game it brings thermal imaging, a stabiliser working in both planes, responsive gun handling and plenty of ammunition types. It is also a big target with little armour and unremarkable mobility, so its best results come from cover, where its fire control advantage tells. It was part of the Chinese ground tree from Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_m8_greyhound: Ford's wartime M8 armoured car served with US and British forces from 1943; in 1949 a few were taken in mainland China, and others went to Taiwan's army, which used them for riot control rather than combat. In the game it is identical to the American M8, with a 37 mm gun and a rear-mounted M2HB that earns its keep against light armour and early aircraft. Aircraft are also its main danger, since strafing runs reach the crew through the open top. It came with Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_m8_scott: Only small numbers of M8 HMCs reached Nationalist China through lend-lease, since Japanese control of the coast made deliveries difficult, and the type may have seen limited action in the Huai Hai campaign. The low-velocity 75 mm howitzer struggles at range, yet its arcing trajectory is also a tool: from behind a low obstacle it can drop shells onto enemies that cannot see it. An M2HB on the roof handles lightly armoured targets and early aircraft. It was introduced in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_m_41d: The M41D was Taiwan's 1990s rebuild of 50 M41A1/A2 Walker Bulldogs, adding a domestic gun able to fire APFSDS, upgraded fire control and an easier-to-maintain engine. The most modern M41 in the game, it has a laser rangefinder, thermal sight and APFSDS but a weaker engine. It is a hull-down sniper: depression and rangefinder suit long shots from cover, poor armour and no stabiliser rule out much else, and brisk reversing gets it away when found. Next to China's PTL02 it reverses better, sits lower and depresses further, but lacks the stabiliser and some firepower. It arrived in the "Winged Lions" update.
cn_mbt2000: NORINCO developed the MBT-2000 for Pakistan, where it is called the Al-Khalid, through the Type 90-II programme; it ended up with a Ukrainian 6TD power pack and was shown as an export product at IDEX 2001. That powertrain sets it apart from the Soviet-derived tanks around it in the Chinese tree, giving T-80UD-like forward speed, unusually quick reverse and neutral steering. The gun matches T-72 equivalents but with better fire control, while protection falls short of tanks like the ZTZ96A, so mobility is its main asset. It joined the game in the "Sons of Attila" update.
cn_mbt2000_sm: This is the MBT-2000, NORINCO's export tank for Pakistan (the Al-Khalid), in a special appearance themed on the character Lin for the 2026 Senrai Maidens event; otherwise it matches the standard version. It brings an autoloading 125 mm gun with modern fire control and a thermal sight, NERA composite armour topped with FY-2 ERA that copes with common APFSDS and HEAT, and a 6TD-2 engine that reverses far better than Soviet designs. The trade-offs are thin sides, ammunition sharing the crew compartment and restricted gun elevation.
cn_object_122tm: Object 122MT was a Chinese second-generation tank prototype of the late 1960s and 1970s, built at the Luoyang Tractor Factory against the Soviet threat and drawing on technology from a captured T-62; work stalled amid the upheaval of the Cultural Revolution and the vehicle remains stored at the factory. Nicknamed the "triple-mechanical" prototype in China, it combined what is described as the world's first 120 mm smoothbore gun with a turret-mounted ATGM, a laser rangefinder and a new diesel engine. It came to the game in the "Danger Zone" update.
cn_object_211: Object 211 was the PLA's late-1950s project for an amphibious tank suited to southern China's rivers and paddy fields, developed with the help of purchased PT-76s and leading to the Type 63; the game models the fourth prototype with the 85 mm Type 63 gun, now kept at Institute 201. It trades protection for pace: the hull barely keeps out machine-gun rounds and shell splinters, but it is low and fast enough to seize good positions at the start, and the 85 mm gun punishes anything it hits squarely. It was added in the "La Royale" update.
cn_oplot_t: Ukraine's T-84 grew out of the T-80UD with a welded turret, and the Oplot-M is its latest production model; Pakistan evaluated it against the VT-4 in 2015–2017 but chose the Chinese tank. In the game it can reverse at 32 km/h, quicker than any other Eastern Bloc design, and its three crew sit behind ERA and NERA with an electrical APS on top. The gun is the weak part, underpowered and short of depression, and gaps such as the one between skirts and hull give opponents targets. It arrived in Update 2.51 "Spearhead" and matches the Thai Oplot-T in Japan's tree.
cn_pgz_04a: The PGZ04A upgrades the PLA's PGZ95 gun-missile SPAA, which grew out of a 1980s requirement shaped by the Italian SIDAM 25, fitting newer MANPADS for the army's close-range air defence layer. In the game it combines four 25 mm cannons, derived from the Shilka's guns but slower-firing with higher velocity and penetration, with a search radar and thermal optics. The missiles are the reason to take it: four HN-6s, a touch better than Stingers, reach aircraft well beyond gun range, making up for electronics, mobility and ground-attack ability that fall short of the newer PGZ09. It came with the "Red Skies" update.
cn_pgz_09: The PGZ09 has defended PLA ground forces since the late 2000s, its 35 mm guns tracing back to the licence-built Oerlikon KDA; the production version dropped the infrared missiles planned for the turret. The game positions it as China's counterpart to the Gepard and Type 87, aimed at helicopters, drones and cruise missiles. It finds and follows targets with its own search and tracking radars, backed by an electro-optical system and second-generation thermals, then engages with 35 mm AHEAD shells that are dangerous to aircraft and unwary ground vehicles; good off-road speed keeps it with the advance. It was introduced in the "Red Skies" update.
cn_pgz_625_fb10: NORINCO's CS/SA5 (Type 625E) pairs a rotary cannon with short-range missiles in a module on a modified ZBL-08 8x8 chassis, aimed at low-flying aircraft, helicopters and drones; it was unveiled at Zhuhai in 2016 and entered service in 2022. Whether used as a dedicated air-defence picket or as a second-line vehicle supporting tanks with its cannon, it has to husband its ammunition and avoid return fire, being large and thinly armoured. It was added in Update 2.47 "Leviathans".
cn_pgz_88: Inspired by the ZSU-23-4's success in 1973, the PGZ88 mounted two 37 mm Type 65 guns and a radar fire control system on a Type 79 tank chassis; unresolved problems limited orders to 24, which now serve the PLA only for training. Its guns fire quickly and their HE shells carry a heavy explosive charge, so aircraft go down fast, while the AP rounds have enough penetration to threaten tanks. Autocannons go straight through its armour, and comparable vehicles generally outpace it. It came with Update 2.57 "Heavy Cavalry".
cn_plz_05: The PLZ05 is the PLA's tracked 155 mm self-propelled howitzer, in service since the early 2000s; it refined the export PLZ45 with a 2S19-derived autoloader, a longer L/52 barrel and a stronger engine. Like the VIDAR, Type 99 and PzH 2000, it puts a fast-firing, high-velocity gun on a tall, lightly armoured hull with sluggish gun handling, and its HE is somewhat weaker than NATO 155 mm rounds. What it adds is a laser rangefinder, a SAP shell for flank shots, a ready rack holding all 30 rounds, spall liners and adjustable suspension that improves effective depression. It arrived in the "Firebirds" update.
cn_plz_45: China began developing the PLZ45 in 1986 as a self-propelled gun for export, basing its 155 mm weapon on the Austrian GHN45 howitzer; after desert trials and revisions it found buyers from 1997 in Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Ethiopia and Algeria, while the PLA only tested a few. In the game its BEA1-155 semi-armour-piercing shell is the main draw, destroying most targets it hits squarely, and HE-VT rounds give it options against aircraft and armour. Otherwise it is a big, slow, thinly armoured gun carriage, with smoke grenades and a commander's heavy machine gun as small consolations. It arrived in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey".
cn_plz_83: The PLZ83 was the PLA's first self-propelled howitzer, a 152 mm design on the purpose-built WZ321 tracked chassis; prototypes appeared in 1980–81, it was certified in late 1983 and first paraded on the 35th National Day. Upgraded with guided shells and datalinks, it and the PLZ83A remain in service until 155 mm systems such as the PLZ05 and PLC181 replace them. It joined the game in the "Kings of Battle" update as China's first domestic SPH, and anyone who has played the 2S3M will find it familiar, since both carry the D-20 (PL66) howitzer.
cn_plz_83_130: NORINCO's PLZ83-130 appeared in a 1987 export catalogue: a PLZ83 with the long-ranged 130 mm PL59A gun in place of the 152 mm howitzer, an idea dropped once the more advanced PLZ45 was ready. Apart from the long 130 mm barrel it mirrors the PLZ83, but its ammunition is more flexible, with a highly penetrating APHE shell, rounds with alternative fuses such as VT, and smoke. It still needs careful positioning, though the 130 mm round's penetration makes it a threat to anything that finds it. It arrived in the "Alpha Strike" update as a reward from the 2024 "Inferno Cannon" event.
cn_pt_76: China bought early-model PT-76 amphibious tanks from the Soviet Union to support Project 211, launched in 1958, which produced the Type 63; because of that early origin, this version lacks the two-plane stabiliser of later PT-76s. In the game it was among the first tanks to receive HEAT-FS, which defeats heavy armour at any range; the catch is the modest calibre, which often needs a second or third hit to finish a target. It came with Update 1.91 "Night Vision" but was taken out of the tech tree in the "La Royale" update, with Object 211 taking its slot; existing owners keep it.
cn_ptl_02: Partly inspired by the French AMX-10RC's use of roads in the Gulf War, the PTL02 became the PLA's first wheeled assault gun, pairing a 100 mm smoothbore with the WZ551 6x6 chassis of the ZSL92; it was certified in 2001. Its gun is the strength: stock APFSDS penetrates 220 mm and the later PT-86-100 up to 381 mm, while a thermal sight and laser rangefinder shorten the time from spotting to killing. With 85 km/h on roads and very thin armour it is a less forgiving flanker than the Centauro or Rooikat Mk.1D, though it still outruns most Chinese tracked vehicles. It arrived in the "Ixwa Strike" update.
cn_ptz_89: Chinese enthusiasts call the PTZ89 the "Eastern Ferdinand": it put an autoloaded 120 mm smoothbore, developed alongside the ZTZ99 programme, onto the WZ321 chassis to blunt Soviet armour, and although already dated on arrival in 1989 it served until 2015, arguably the last gun-armed tank destroyer built. In the game it resembles the Soviet Object 120 in concept but meets nimble opposition like the Leopard A1A1 without matching their speed or armour. Its strength lies entirely in a 120 mm gun that few targets can resist and a fast loading cycle for dealing with several enemies at once, so it suits sniping and ambush positions. It came with the "New Power" update.
cn_qn506: Unveiled at Zhuhai in 2018 under the nickname "New King of Land Warfare", the QN506 rebuilds a ZTZ59 chassis with a 30 mm turret, missiles and crew camera systems, pitched against Russia's BMPT for urban and counter-insurgency work; no export customer has ordered it yet. It was the first vehicle in ground battles to carry fire-and-forget missiles, arriving as a main prize of the "Repair Factory" event in the "Sky Guardians" update. Its ZTZ59 roots show in its protection and mobility, but the combination of a 30 mm cannon and 24 guided missiles lets it threaten air and ground targets alike.
cn_sdkfz_222_early: Horch-built Sd.Kfz.222 armoured cars reached Nationalist China with the 1933 German arms shipments, giving fire support to reconnaissance units alongside the machine-gun-only Sd.Kfz.221; this early model differs from the German army's in its tyres and gun system. It gives China's early ground line-up a rare fast autocannon car. Flanking is essential, because the cannon cannot get through many of the early light tanks it meets; on the other hand, the gun elevates high enough to engage aircraft. It was added in the "Sky Guardians" update.
cn_su_100_1945: When Soviet forces left Dalian in December 1950, they sold the 99 SU-100s based there to China, where they equipped the PLA's new 1st Mechanized Division and were used heavily for ambushes in Korea. In the game its 100 mm D-10S reloads much faster than the guns of the ISU-122 and ISU-152, making it better at dealing with tanks. Ambush suits it here too: the vehicle sits low enough to hide in tall vegetation, and its steeply angled front helps when it is found. It came with Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_su_76m_1943: The SU-76M mounted the ZIS-3 divisional gun on a stretched T-70 chassis and was the Soviet Union's second most-produced armoured vehicle of the war after the T-34; between 1951 and 1954 the PLA bought 912 for its infantry divisions' self-propelled artillery regiments. Its 76 mm gun, able to defeat most opponents from the front, outguns the captured and lend-lease tanks it sits among in the early Chinese tree. Aircraft are the main danger: the fighting compartment is open and there is no machine gun to fire back. It arrived in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_t_26_1940: Soviet-supplied T-26 Model 1933s equipped the Nationalist 200th Mechanized Division in the war against Japan, fighting from Shanghai to Burma and later in the civil war; a few survivors were apparently taken to Taiwan before vanishing from the records. The Chinese example matches the Soviet T-26. Armour is weak for a light tank, so the 45 mm gun does its work best from ambush or the flanks, and as a first tank it teaches habits that carry over to everything later. It came with Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_t_26_no531: Number 531 was the command T-26 of General Sun Li-jen, the tactician nicknamed the "Rommel of the East", whose 200th Division used some of the 82 T-26s China bought in 1937–1938 and later beat the Japanese in Burma in 1943; he was afterwards accused of spying and spent years under house arrest in Taiwan. Apart from its camouflage it is the tech-tree T-26, a small, slow and fragile tank whose good gun rewards shooting from cover at range, and new players learn quickly that exposure is punished. It was introduced in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_t_34_1942: China got only a few Model 1943 T-34s from the Soviet Union during the war, plus some abandoned after the Soviet invasion of Manchuria, but the type saw very little Chinese use, with the PLA relying mainly on the T-34-85 instead. It has a strong balance of cross-country speed, armour and firepower, and in experienced hands it remains dangerous, though from the Panzer IV F2 onwards German guns can punish it. It came with Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_t_34_85_d_5t: This T-34-85 Model 1944 carries the easier-to-load ZiS S-53 gun, with the radio moved into the turret and a better gunner's sight; China received 300 as Soviet aid during the Korean War, where they formed the People's Volunteer Army's main armoured force. The 85 mm gun is a big step up from the T-34 (1943). Most opponents at its level can still punch through the sloped armour, so drawn-out exchanges are best avoided, and anyone wanting a roof heavy machine gun should look to the T-34-85 Gai. It arrived in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_t_34_85_zis_53_no215: Tank No.215 is a celebrated Chinese T-34-85: in July 1953, near Pork Chop Hill, its crew camouflaged it after it bogged down, ambushed American tanks the next day and knocked out more while withdrawing, part of a war record that earned it the title "People's Hero Tank". It is now a museum exhibit in Beijing. Performance is identical to the T-34-85 (S-53): the 85 mm gun is a real upgrade over earlier T-34s, the armour gives way to most guns it meets, and there is no roof machine gun. It was sold during the 2020 Lunar New Year sale in Update 1.95 "Northern Wind".
cn_t_62: T-62 No.545 was disabled by Chinese artillery fire and mines in the 1969 Damansky/Zhenbao Island clash; Soviet guns then sank it, but Chinese forces raised it with navy divers a month later for study, and its technology fed into revisions of the Type 69. It plays exactly like the Soviet T-62, differing only in its turret number, Chinese camouflages and missing spare track mounts, so its 115 mm smoothbore far outclasses the Type 69's gun. Sold as a store pack from Update 1.91 "Night Vision" until May 2020, it returned for in-game purchase during Lunar New Year events.
cn_t_80ud_478be: Pakistan bought 320 Ukrainian T-80UDs in 1996 to bridge the gap until its MBT-2000 programme was ready, receiving them between 1997 and 1999; some were Object 478BE models without the IR searchlight and with a turret closer to the T-84's. Added as a main prize of the "Winter Tales" event, it brings the T-80 line to the Chinese tree. It looks almost the same as the Russian T-80UD and keeps its mobility, but a high-definition thermal sight makes spotting targets far easier. The older 6TD engine reverses slowly, so advancing needs care, and kinetic ammunition tops out at 3BM42.
cn_tor_m1: China's ground and air force air-defence units bought the Tor-M1 (SA-15) from Russia in the late 1990s to meet a need for field air defence, and later developed an improved copy, the HQ-17. Eight missiles with a long reach and sustained motor thrust, cued by a long-range search radar, make it a capable anti-aircraft vehicle in the game. It has trouble with targets at very steep angles, beyond about 75 degrees, and its size and launch trails give its position away at once. It arrived in the "Fire and Ice" update.
cn_type_58: The T-34-85 Gai represents a planned Chinese production version of the T-34-85 from the 1950s, with a heavy machine gun on the commander's cupola and small external changes; it was dropped once T-54A blueprints led to the Type 59, and the existing T-34-85s went into reserve until the 1990s. In the game it handles like the Soviet-built T-34-85. Its distinguishing feature is a 12.7 mm DShK on the roof, the first time a T-34 in the game gets a heavy machine gun of this kind. It came with Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_type_59: Built under licence from the T-54A from 1958, the Type 59 served as the PLA's backbone for over four decades, receiving new fire control, guns and protection along the way before newer domestic tanks replaced it this century. Visually it resembles the T-54 (1951) more than the T-54A, apart from its fume extractor and T-55A-style road wheels, and it has a single-plane stabiliser and different ammunition from the Soviet tank. Time spent mastering it carries over to its descendants, the Type 69, ZTZ59D1 and T-69 II G. It was part of the original Chinese tree from Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_type_59d: Certified in April 1995, the ZTZ59D1 was the prototype for the ZTZ59D, an economical upgrade of the Type 59 with FY-1/2 ERA and digital fire control. In the game it swaps the old 100 mm gun for a licence-built 105 mm L7 and adds explosive reactive armour, a laser rangefinder and night sights, a big gain in firepower. The old hull still limits it, with slow movement and gun handling, which makes it a poor fit for the quick brawls common at its level; a patient player sniping from range gets far more from it. It came with Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_type_62: Designed from 1958 and in production from 1963 to 1989, with about 1,500 built, the Type 62 is a lightened Type 59 with a smaller gun, thinner armour and less equipment, intended for the rugged, mountainous south of China. Being small and nimble, it is at home on overgrown, broken maps, slipping into positions opponents do not expect and ambushing from them, while the 85 mm Type 63 gun and generous ammunition supply let it take shots at any range. It arrived in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_type_63_I: The Type 63 was China's first amphibious tank, developed from the Soviet PT-76 by factories 201 and 617, finalised in 1963 and in service from 1964; it went to North Vietnam during the Vietnam War and saw limited use in the 1979 war with Vietnam. Little armour and no two-plane stabiliser (unlike later PT-76s) make it a stop-and-shoot vehicle, but the Type 62's turret gives it far more firepower than the PT-76, including HEAT-FS rated at 300 mm of penetration. It came with Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_type_64: Short of light tank replacements in the 1970s, Taiwan's army combined M42 Duster hulls with M18 turrets to make the M64, converting 42 alongside the M65, a local copy of the M41; they were never used in action and retired in the 1980s, with only a few preserved. In the game it is heavier than the M18, but a stronger engine keeps its mobility similar. It was a Battle Pass Season VI "Firepower" reward in the "Winged Lions" update.
cn_type_65_aa: This North Vietnamese improvisation from the mid-1960s fitted a T-34-85 hull with an open, box-shaped turret carrying two Chinese 37 mm Type 65 guns; the only known example was captured by US forces and is displayed at Fort Sill, and the name was invented for the game since the real designation is unknown. It can both defend against aircraft and flank ground targets, helped by a quick-turning turret, a reasonable rate of fire and HVAP rounds, but its armour barely keeps out rifle-calibre fire and a nearby HE burst can finish it. It came with Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_type_69: The original Type 69 was a 1974 batch of 100 tanks meant to replace the Type 59, influenced by the captured T-62 No.545 and fitted with a 100 mm smoothbore that disappointed in trials; the rifled Type 69-II became the service model instead. In the game it mixes T-55A-like mobility and gun handling with a T-62-style smoothbore firing HEATFS and APFSDS, plus night vision, a two-plane stabiliser and a laser rangefinder. Next to the Type 59 the faster turret and better stabilisation are welcome, but a weak APFSDS replaces dependable APHE, so firepower is no real improvement. It came with Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_type_69_2a: The Type 69-IIa went back to a rifled 100 mm gun and became NORINCO's flagship export of the 1980s, bought in thousands by Iran and Iraq thanks to its low price. In the game it compares with the T-55A and shares many shells with it. From the Type 59 it takes the rifled gun and APHEBC; from the Type 69, the laser rangefinder, night sights, stronger engine and faster turret; and it adds smoke grenades, with improved fire control suiting long-range fights. First a Chinese-server event gift, it reached international servers in the "Drone Age" update and has since been sold during National Day events.
cn_type_69_2g: The T-69 II G is Bangladesh's late-2000s upgrade of its Type 69s, adding a long 105 mm gun, ERA on the upper front plate and turret and probably improved optics; it was first seen during the 2009 BDR mutiny. Its ERA often stops HEATFS and missiles from lower-ranked tanks, though armour and mobility are otherwise ordinary, and the high-velocity gun hits hard, making it a good partner for the similar ZTZ59D1. Slow reloading and reactions mean it is better brought out later in a match and should disable a target with the opening shot. It was first sold as a store pack in the "Starfighters" update.
cn_type_86: The ZBD86 was China's reverse-engineered BMP-1, developed from an Egyptian example, certified in 1986 and later upgraded with 25 and 30 mm turrets as the ZBD86-I and ZBD86A. Stock, it is almost identical to the Soviet BMP-1 apart from missing the turret-side canvas rolls. The "ZBD86 Late" modification is the reason to use it: it adds the HJ-73E, a SACLOS development of the Malyutka with a tandem warhead that can destroy any target the vehicle meets, whether or not it carries ERA or composite armour. It came with Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_type_97_chi_ha: Around 300 ex-Japanese Chi-Ha tanks were passed to the Chinese communists by the USSR after 1945 and equipped the PLA's first tank unit, the Northeast Tank Brigade; unreliable enough to be nicknamed the "Old Man Tank", they still fought at Jinzhou and Tianjin. Like other Japanese designs it has good gun depression but little armour, and its low-velocity 57 mm gun was built to support infantry rather than fight tanks, so the Chinese tree's first medium tank needs a careful, cautious approach. It came with Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_type_97_kai: On 1 December 1945, Gao Ke of the Northeast People's Autonomous Army seized two Chi-Ha Kai tanks from a Japanese repair works in Shenyang; numbered 101 and 102, they marked the founding of the Northeast Tank Brigade, and more ex-Japanese tanks later came to the PLA from the Soviets. Its main gain over the original Chi-Ha in the game is much better anti-tank capability, and it makes a quick, adaptable medium tank for the early Chinese line-up. It came with Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_vt_4: NORINCO's VT4 (MBT-3000) is an export development of the MBT-2000 that borrows parts such as FY-2 ERA from China's own service tanks and gains a 1,200 hp engine and automatic transmission; Thailand, Nigeria and Pakistan have bought it, the last ordering 680. In the game its ZPT-98A gun reloads in 6.7 seconds and can fire the high-penetration DTC10-125. Reversing at 17 km/h, it is slower backwards than the MBT-2000 but quicker than most Chinese and Soviet tanks. Its armour is middling, with tough sections but weak areas large enough for anyone to hit. It arrived in Update 2.49 "Tusk Force".
cn_vt_4b: The VT4A1 is NORINCO's top export tank, an update of the VT4 shown at Zhuhai in 2022 and fitted with the GL-6 hard-kill APS and a micro-drone for scouting; the VT4 line uses an all-Chinese power pack derived from the ZTZ99A after Ukraine threatened to withhold its 6TD-2 engines. The A1 has yet to win an export order. In the game it sits lower than the WZ1001-based tanks without giving up much in armour or mobility, fires the same rounds as the PLA's own MBTs and can swat incoming projectiles with its APS. It arrived in the "Air Superiority" update.
cn_vt_5: The VT5 is NORINCO's export light tank, marketed as a "lightweight MBT" for terrain such as floodplains and high plateaus where heavier tanks struggle; Bangladesh is so far the only buyer, taking 140 to replace its upgraded Type 59 and 69 fleets, and the game models that Bangladeshi variant. Opponents may take it lightly because of its class, but its rapid reload lets it keep firing effectively at all ranges, which quickly makes it a priority target. It was added in the "Hornet's Sting" update.
cn_wma_301: NORINCO's WMA301 is an export alternative to the PTL02, built on the same WZ551 chassis but with an arrowhead welded turret reminiscent of the ZTZ96A and a 105 mm rifled gun; it has served in several African countries and Myanmar as a fast-response vehicle. Handling is close to the PTL02; what changes is the gun. Its best APFSDS falls short of the PTL02's top round, yet the rifled 105 mm adds proximity-fused HE for helicopters and the GP105, a tandem-warhead missile fired from the barrel that deals with heavily armoured targets. It came with the "Red Skies" update.
cn_wz_1001: The WZ1001(E) LCT (Long Cannon Testbed) was the second prototype in the programme that produced the ZTZ99A, pairing a longer L/54 125 mm gun with a ZTZ99-III-based hull; cost and gun reliability concerns saw it dropped in favour of the L/48 version. In the game it performs almost like the ZTZ99A, with better gun handling from its experimental gun-laying system and a higher muzzle velocity. Its hybrid build, a ZTZ99 hull under a turret resembling the ZTZ99A's, also brings together the weak points of each, so despite its strong mobility it pays to think before charging in. It arrived in the "Apex Predators" update.
cn_wz_141: The WZ141-1 was a mid-1970s Chinese prototype for a light, air-droppable tank destroyer that could be landed behind Soviet lines or carried on ordinary trucks; it mounted two Type 75 105 mm recoilless rifles derived from the American M40, and the project was cancelled in 1985. In the game the twin rifles fire high-penetration HEAT-FS that can kill many targets even from the front, though the turret turns slowly and the guns barely depress. Speed makes it one of the best flankers at its level, which matters, as the aluminium hull keeps out nothing heavier than small-arms fire. It was a reward from Battle Pass Season XX, "Flying Dragon".
cn_wz_305: The WZ305 placed a twin-gun turret modelled on the ZSU-57-2 onto a ZTZ79 chassis to give the PLA heavy-calibre field air defence; outclassed by modern jets, it was never adopted at home but was exported to the Middle East. ZSU-57-2 players will feel at home, though its Type 69-derived hull has thicker armour, about three tonnes more weight and a slightly stronger engine. The big advantage is the DKY-1 airburst HE shell, which makes it far more effective against aircraft, and it can also pick off light vehicles and cover flanks. It came with Update 1.95 "Northern Wind".
cn_zbd_04a: The ZBD04A is the PLA's most advanced IFV, first seen in 2011; it kept the ZBD04's turret but moved to a Western-influenced hull with better protection, mobility and fire control. In the game it finally gives China an autocannon IFV. Good fire control, a broad mix of Chinese and licensed BMP-3-pattern ammunition and surprising agility for a large vehicle let it either flank or follow an attack in support. Its size is the drawback, making hard cover essential when a fight turns against it. It arrived in the "Alpha Strike" update.
cn_zsd63_pg87: This makeshift SPAA puts twin PG87 25 mm cannons on the ZSD63, China's first domestic APC, which entered service in 1970 and saw use in Vietnam; the conversion probably dates from the 1990s. Despite its improvised look it hits very hard, shredding aircraft and light vehicles and even threatening medium tanks with AP rounds, and its high-velocity shells make aiming easy. The catch is ammunition: both 40-round magazines empty in about four seconds, reloading takes over 30, and there are only five reloads. Being big, tall and thinly armoured, it is also easy to kill. It came with the "Starfighters" update.
cn_zsl_92: The ZSL92 was the first mass-produced member of the WZ551 wheeled family, developed by Factory 256 from a Mercedes-Benz truck-based concept and later the basis for the PTL02, WMA301 and AFT09. In the game its 25 mm cannon, the same as the ZSD63/PG87's, can be raised high enough for aircraft and will defeat most contemporaries side-on. The thin hull and weak reverse gear leave no easy way out of trouble, so it pays to plan any push in advance. It arrived in the "Seek & Destroy" update.
cn_ztl_11: The ZLT11 is the PLA's 8x8 wheeled assault gun, China's answer to the US Army's MGS, built on the ZBL08 chassis with a turret likely derived from the ZTD05; certified in 2011, it serves with mechanised and marine brigades and has been exported to Africa as the ST1. In the game it reaches 100 km/h, can swim at 9 km/h and carries a 105 mm gun firing powerful APFSDS as well as barrel-launched missiles, plus second-generation thermals for the gunner. Better protected than the PTL02, it is the first Chinese wheeled vehicle that stands comparison with NATO equivalents. It came in Update 2.11 "Ground Breaking".
cn_zts_63_1980: From 1980 the ZTS63 amphibious tank, called simply the Type 63 until 1987, gained a laser rangefinder and improved fire control borrowed from the ZTZ59A and ZTQ62, and it supported Chinese troops in the Sino-Vietnamese fighting of the early 1980s. It handles exactly like the Type 62 and Type 63, but better fire control, a DShK machine gun and APFSDS, together with the rangefinder, greatly extend its reach. Armour that struggles even against heavy machine guns and a sluggish turret remain its weak points. It arrived in the "Sky Guardians" update.
cn_ztz_59a: Certified in 1984, the ZTZ59A was the first major upgrade of the PLA's Type 59, prompted by lessons from the war with Vietnam: it gained a laser rangefinder, fire control with automatic ballistic calculation, an IR searchlight, side skirts, smoke launchers and new APFSDS. In the game it carries some Type 69 technology onto the dated Type 59 chassis. Compared with the standard Type 59 it is a clear step up, chiefly because the rangefinder makes long shots practical and smoke offers a way out of trouble. It joined the game in the "Ground Breaking" update.
cn_ztz_88a: The ZTZ88A was a late-1990s revision of the ZTZ88, itself developed from the ZTZ80 to bridge the gap before the ZTZ99, with a longer ZPL94 105 mm gun and trial appliqué composite armour; about 700 were built alongside the ZTZ88B. In the game it bridges the ZTZ59/69 family and the ZTZ96, whose engine it introduces, with better fire control and the long 105 mm. It outpaces anything built on the T-54, but Soviet MBTs shrug off more kinetic rounds and NATO tanks are more adaptable; its value lies in preparing players for the Chinese MBTs that follow. It arrived in the "Wind of Change" update.
cn_ztz_88b: The ZTZ88B was the first mass-produced tank of the WZ122 family, which traces back to the cancelled Object 122 work; it combined the ZTZ85 hull with the ZTZ80-I turret as a stopgap until the ZTZ99 was ready, and appeared at the 50th National Day Parade. In the game it is closely related to the ZTZ88A. Coming from the ZTZ59/69, players will notice a faster gun-laying system and a 730 hp engine that helps in every direction, while trial appliqué armour adds protection against kinetic and chemical rounds alike. It came with the "La Royale" update.
cn_ztz_96: The ZTZ96 married a ZTZ88-derived hull to the turret of the Type 85-IIM export tank, adding domestic fire control; it has been in PLA service for close to 30 years and led to upgrades such as the ERA-equipped ZTZ96A. It looks like a T-72 in layout but has a flat, angular welded turret and a bigger hull with smaller road wheels, with composite armour in the turret cheeks and upper glacis. The autoloaded 125 mm has a limited choice of rounds, though its APFSDS and HE deal with most targets, and neither its armour nor its mobility rises above ordinary. It arrived in Update 1.93 "Shark Attack".
cn_ztz_96a: Entering service in 2005, the ZTZ96A gave the ZTZ96 new fire control, protection and power as a cheaper partner to the ZTZ99; the arrowhead-armour prototype beat a needle-nosed rival, and older ZTZ96s cannot be brought up to this standard. The game version wraps the hull and turret in FY-4 ERA, which hugely improves resistance to both kinetic penetrators and HEAT, and adds a thermal sight for the gunner and a little more engine power. It still trails the best tanks in mobility and armour, yet it is adaptable enough to hold its own. It came with Update 1.97 "Viking Fury".
cn_ztz_96a_prot: This needle-nosed prototype lost out to the arrowhead design that became the ZTZ96A, and it disappeared from the record apart from a few photographs. Its turret carries spaced high-hardness armour in a pointed, Chieftain-like profile instead of the production ERA mount, giving up some protection. In exchange it gets two JD-3 jammers on the turret sides, a soft-kill system similar to the T-90A's Shtora that disrupts ATGM guidance. Otherwise it matches the production tank, thermal sight and strong gun included. It arrived in the "Wind of Change" update.
cn_ztz_96b: Unusually, the ZTZ96B was built to do better in Tank Biathlon competitions rather than in combat, after the ZTZ96A disappointed there in mobility, reliability and accuracy; unveiled in 2016, it got a stronger engine, refined transmission, upgraded gun and fire control, and only small numbers were made. In the game it moves and shoots as well as most rivals, but a sluggish reload and a front riddled with weak spots call for careful use of cover, and the tightly packed interior means one penetration is often fatal. It arrived in Update 2.55 "Ninth Wave".
cn_ztz_99: The ZTZ99-II is the PLA's accepted ZTZ99 configuration: work on a third-generation tank began in 1984, drawing on study of the T-72 and T-80U, and the early-production tanks shown at the 50th National Day Parade received FY-4 ERA on the hull front and turret in 2004. The design mixes Western-style arrowhead turret armour with Soviet-style ERA, and in the game its fire control and handling outshine most Soviet tanks. Weak spots at the driver's hatch, mantlet and lower plate, along with a long hull, mean it still needs careful play. It came with the "Hot Tracks" update.
cn_ztz_99_w: Finalised in 2004, the ZTZ99-III revised the ZTZ99's turret and hull with an extended turret bustle, a welded turret and rearranged ERA, becoming the standard version; it led the 2009 National Day Parade and serves mostly in northern China and on the Tibetan Plateau. It plays like the ZTZ99-II with some of that tank's weak points tidied up, while gun, speed and frontal armour stay the same. China has more advanced tanks, but this is a dependable one. It arrived in the "Direct Hit" update.
cn_ztz_99a: The ZTZ99A, product of the WZ1001 programme, has led the PLA's tank force since the 2010s; it first appeared publicly at the September 2015 victory parade and abandoned the low profile of earlier Chinese tanks. In the game it has a bigger turret and new power pack while keeping protection similar to the ZTZ99-III, and its strong mobility is the key to using it well. It came with the "Danger Zone" update.
corsair_fmk2: The Corsair F Mk II was the Fleet Air Arm's lend-lease F4U-1A, its wings clipped by 0.36 m to fit British carrier hangars; 510 were delivered, serving in the Pacific as both fighters and strike aircraft. In the game six Browning M2s, good durability and a high top speed for its level make it a strong dogfighter, held back by modest agility and an average climb. Against ground targets it can use its guns or carry one 500 lb or 1,000 lb bomb. It arrived in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
cr_32: Celestino Rosatelli's CR.32 developed the CR.30 with a revised engine installation and two 12.7 mm Breda-SAFAT guns, and the Regia Aeronautica valued its balance of agility and firepower across several campaigns. It is the first aircraft in the Italian tree. In the game it fights by turning, staying agile even when slow, and its two heavy machine guns are deadly, above all with air-target belts; the downside is an airframe that gives way after a few hits. It came with Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica".
cr_32_bis: The CR.32 bis added two 7.7 mm machine guns at some cost in speed and agility; 328 were built in 1936–37, and they did well in the Spanish Civil War against the I-15 and I-16 before the CR.42 replaced them. It flies like other biplanes, turning tightly with a low stall speed but a weak engine, poor energy retention and a slow roll, and its 12.7 mm guns are deadly to biplanes and can still hurt early monoplanes such as the Hurricane; in simulator its telescopic sight is a real handicap. Originally a pre-order pack for Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica", it later returned through the Warbonds shop.
cr_32_quater: The CR.32 quater was a lightened version meant to improve low-altitude agility and the last of the series built before production ended in 1939; it equipped several Italian fighter units, including squadrons in East Africa, when the war began. It is the second reserve aircraft of the Italian tree. Compared with the CR.32 it is more agile but no better armed: the same two 12.7 mm guns, whose incendiary-rich air-targets belt is very good at starting fires. It came with Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica".
cw_21: The CW-21 was a lightweight interceptor developed from the CW-19 for climb and high-altitude work; China took three complete aircraft and 27 kits, and the Dutch used the CW-21B, but in combat it proved easy prey for Japanese fighters and prone to structural cracks. In the game its climb rate is outstanding, letting it outclimb most opponents and stay competitive even against stronger aircraft such as the A6M2 and P-51. Two .50 and two .30 calibre guns lack cannon punch but have plenty of ammunition and range, and it out-turns most aircraft apart from biplanes and Japanese fighters. It came with Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
d3a1: The Aichi D3A1, the Imperial Japanese Navy's Type 99 Carrier Dive Bomber, was the first Japanese aircraft to strike American targets, at Pearl Harbor, and flew in most early carrier operations including the Coral Sea and Midway; no Axis aircraft sank more Allied ships, though losses mounted as Allied fighters improved. In the game it carries one 250 kg and two 60 kg bombs, with two forward guns and a rear gunner. It is tough but neither quick, at about 440 km/h, nor agile by Japanese standards; its strength is accuracy in the dive, aided by air brakes. It has been in the game since the open beta.
d4y1: The D4Y1 Suisei was designed to succeed the D3A1 with enough speed to escape pursuers and the range to outreach American carriers, using the Atsuta 21, a licence-built DB 601; that engine outperformed Japanese designs but proved hard to build and maintain. In the game the emphasis on speed and range leaves it fragile and limited to a single bomb of up to 500 kg, so its role is to strike quickly and leave. It arrived in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
d4y2: The Suisei 12 replaced the D4Y1's Atsuta 21 with the Atsuta 31, simpler to look after and about 200 hp stronger, but engine supply problems persisted and many airframes sat finished without engines. In the game it is faster than the D4Y1, and the extra power lets it carry either two 60 kg bombs or four rockets under the wings. The rockets work against ground targets or aircraft, where a distance fuse lets them catch large, slow bombers with near misses if the range is judged correctly. It arrived in Update 1.71 "New E.R.A.".
d4y3: Because licence-built DB 601 engines were scarce, the D4Y3 Suisei 33 switched to the plentiful Kinsei 62 radial, but the new nose added drag, so the inline Model 12 stayed in production for priority units. In the game that drag puts it between the D4Y2 and D4Y1 in performance. Its real advantage is the Ko sub-variant's rear 13 mm Type 2 heavy machine gun, replacing the 7.7 mm Type 92, which makes attacking it from behind far riskier. It came with Update 1.71 "New E.R.A.".
d_371: First flown in 1934, the D.371 was the first production model of Dewoitine's D.37 family: a parasol-wing monoplane with fixed undercarriage, a Gnome-Rhône 14Kfs engine and an open cockpit, obsolete before it could see combat. In the game speed management is everything: with energy it is a quick, agile turn fighter, without it an easy kill. Four MAC 1934 guns make up in volume what each lacks in hitting power. As a starter aircraft it regularly meets faster opponents, and its best answer is to lure them into a turning contest. It came with Update 1.73 "Vive la France".
d_371_hs9: This experimental D.371 was fitted with two Hispano-Suiza HS.9 20 mm cannons. Flown with its speed kept up, it is an agile turn fighter like the standard version. The cannons wreck early aircraft, many of them built of wood and fabric, but with only 30 rounds per gun each burst must count. It was a premium pack in Update 1.73 "Vive la France", withdrawn after the 2018 Victory Day sale, and later returned as a reward for the game's 7th and 10th anniversaries.
d_373: The D.373 is the navalised member of Dewoitine's D.37 family, a parasol-wing fighter with a tail hook for carrier landings, four Darne Mle 33 7.5 mm machine guns, wheel brakes, no armour and an open cockpit. In the game it shares the D.371's character: it turns very well while it keeps its speed up and is easy prey once it slows down. The Darne guns are light, but four of them fill the air with bullets, and against the faster aircraft it often meets, a turning fight is its best hope. It arrived in Update 1.73 "Vive la France".
d_500: Dewoitine's all-metal D.500 replaced the ageing NiD-62 in French service from 1935, but newer types like the M.S.406 soon outclassed it; it saw no combat in the Battle of France and the D.520 succeeded it. Cockpit visibility is excellent, blocked only where the wings meet the fuselage, which helps in simulator and cockpit view. Four machine guns share 1,200 rounds and do serious damage, particularly with convergence set between 150 and 350 m. It came with Update 1.73 "Vive la France".
d_501: The D.501 was a D.500 variant whose Hispano-Suiza 12Xcrs engine made room for a 20 mm cannon firing alongside a pair of machine guns, an unusually strong armament at a time when most fighters carried two light machine guns. A total of 160 were built before the Second World War, and they saw very little front-line service. It was added in Update 1.73 "Vive la France".
d_510: This premium D.510 carries the markings of French pilot Gabriel Pallier. Dewoitine's open-cockpit monoplane is armed with a Hispano-Suiza HS.404 cannon and two MAC 1934 7.5 mm machine guns. In the game it is an all-round average performer whose one notable flaw is an engine that ignites very readily, particularly when struck by 12.7 mm rounds. It is the starting premium of the French air tree, added in Update 1.73 "Vive la France" and given away in the 2017 Christmas event.
d_510c: In 1937 China's Nationalist government looked to Europe for new fighters, and France agreed to sell 34 D.510s, but only 24 arrived by 1938 before Japanese blockades closed the routes; flown by Chinese and European pilots, they achieved little before Soviet and American fighters replaced them by 1941. A 20 mm cannon gives it unusually heavy firepower for its level and it turns tightly, but it has little protection, limited ammunition and an engine that feels dated against higher-ranked opponents. This premium came with the "Danger Zone" update.
d_520: The Dewoitine D.520 first flew in October 1938, but delays meant units only received it after the war had started; it fought reasonably well, then served Vichy France and later Germany, Italy and Bulgaria, mostly as a trainer, with French survivors training pilots until 1953. This version sat in the British tree from the open beta until its French-tree counterpart replaced it in Update 1.73 "Vive la France". Its strengths are agility, a hard-hitting cannon and fair armour; its weaknesses are a low top speed, an average climb and machine guns that do little unless the cannon is firing too.
d_520_france: Widely regarded as one of France's best wartime fighters, the D.520 used a Hispano-Suiza 12Y engine, a 20 mm cannon and four MAC 1934 machine guns, and fought for both Vichy and Free French forces, in 1940 and in Syria in 1941. In the game a fair turn time is let down by a slow climb and low top speed, so it is best flown with height in hand, diving on targets and keeping energy to escape. Its 60 cannon rounds go quickly, whereas the machine guns have ammunition to spare but little effect on twin-engined aircraft and bombers. It came with Update 1.73 "Vive la France".
d_521: The D.521 was a single D.520 re-engined with a Rolls-Royce Merlin III and given slightly different armament. In the game the Merlin brings a modest gain in power, but extra weight takes the edge off its turn and climb, so it ends up an all-rounder without a standout trait. Flying it well comes down to knowing the opposing aircraft and picking fights carefully. It was a gift aircraft in the British tree, awarded for the 2013 "Vive la Liberté!" video contest and the 2014 "First Flight of Dewoitine D.520" event.
db_3a_china: Between 24 and 30 DB-3s reached China as Soviet aid in June 1939 and became known for raids on the Japanese-held Wangjiadun airfield at Wuhan that autumn, reported to have destroyed over 100 aircraft; they served until larger types such as the B-24 replaced them. Its 2.1-tonne bomb capacity is large for its level, and strong forward gun coverage makes head-on passes unattractive for attackers, though cannon-armed fighters can still take it apart quickly. It came with Update 1.91 "Night Vision" as part of the original Chinese air tree.
db_3b: Ilyushin's DB-3 entered Soviet service in 1936 and became the backbone of the long-range bomber force, carrying up to 2,000 kg of bombs and three ShKAS guns, and it flew night raids deep into German territory early in the war; the DB-3B fitted more powerful M-87 engines. In the game its varied loadouts let it switch between bombing bases, attacking ships and other tasks, which makes up for modest speed. Clumsy handling is what fighters exploit. It arrived in Update 1.67 "Assault".
db_lk: Viktor Belyayev's DB-LK of 1939 was an experimental bomber with twin booms on a large "bat wing", designed for payload and range; the sole prototype flew over Red Square on May Day 1940, but a tail-heavy balance, long take-off runs, poor cockpit visibility and inferiority to the DB-3 and Pe-2 ended the programme. Its bomb options range from swarms of small bombs for bases and carpet bombing to two 1,000 kg bombs. Weak engines and the rearward centre of gravity make take-off a struggle, especially when loaded, and the turrets leave blind spots, the worst directly astern. It arrived in Update 2.53 "Line of Contact".
dh_110_sea_vixen: de Havilland's DH.110 lost both Royal Navy and RAF competitions after a prototype broke up at an air show, killing 31 people, but the company kept developing it and the navy ordered 148 as the Sea Vixen, entering service in 1959; accidents claimed over a third of the fleet and it saw almost no combat. In the game few opponents can both turn and run with it. It has no guns and rolls slowly, but its Red Top missiles handle most targets other than flare-carrying A-4Es, and bombs, rockets and AGM-12B Bullpups make it a versatile premium. It came with the "Red Skies" update.
do_17e_1: Dornier's Do 17, nicknamed the "flying pencil" for its slim fuselage, was conceived as a fast bomber and served from the Spanish Civil War into the Second World War; the E-1 used two BMW VI V12 engines. Speed is its protection in the game: with a 640 km/h dive limit it can leave many pursuing fighters behind, which matters because the two single 7.92 mm guns above and below have narrow arcs and little stopping power. The price of the slim fuselage is a bomb load of only 500 kg. It came with Update 1.51 "Cold Steel".
do_17z_2: The Do 17 Z, developed in 1938 from Spanish Civil War experience, grouped the whole crew in a single enlarged nose cabin for better survivability and defence, and the Z-2's Bramo 323 P engines with two-stage superchargers restored a 1,000 kg bomb load. It was used early in the war against infrastructure, shipping and front-line targets. In the game it improves on the Do 17 E-1 with stronger defensive guns, a heavier bomb load and better flight performance, and like other medium bombers it is well suited to destroying bases, vehicles and ships. It arrived in Update 1.53 "Firestorm".
do_17z_7: The Do 17 Z-7 Kauz I turned obsolete Do 17 bombers into night fighters from 1940, intercepting bombers at low altitude while remaining able to support ground troops, and they were used widely against Allied raids. In the game it keeps the bomber's speed, enough to outpace most early aircraft though not later monoplanes, and also its limits: a poor climb, sluggish handling and wings that can fail under hard manoeuvring. Its nose guns, however, can destroy any opponent, and it can carry the E-1's small bombs for ground attack. It came with Update 1.53 "Firestorm".
do_217e_2: The Do 217 E grew out of the Do 17 as a medium bomber with two BMW 801 radials, the engine of the Fw 190, and up to 4,000 kg of bombs; it entered combat in 1941 and served to the end of the war. In the game it is faster than most bombers it meets and can wreck several targets per sortie with C250 incendiaries or four SC 1000s, whose large blast also suits close air support. F5W torpedoes are available too, and a fixed forward cannon can catch distracted fighters or bombers. A 700 km/h structural limit lets it dive away from Spitfires and Yaks. It came in Update 1.29.
do_217e_4: The E-4 differed from the E-2 mainly in its BMW 801L engines and a 20 mm MG FF/M cannon in place of the forward 7.92 mm gun, with a five-man crew and the same 4,000 kg bomb capacity. In the game it shares the E-2's strengths: good speed for a bomber, enough ordnance (C250 incendiaries, SC 1000s or F5W torpedoes) to take out several targets in one run, and a dive limit high enough to escape fighters such as Spitfires and Yaks. The forward cannon can also punish careless fighters or bombers. It came in Update 1.29.
do_217j_1: Developed in 1941 because the Luftwaffe found its Ju 88s and Bf 110s inadequate as night interceptors, the J-1 packed four 20 mm MG FF cannons and four 7.92 mm MG 17s into the nose of the Do 217; 130 were built in 1942–43. Its nose battery can shred almost anything it catches. Catching things is the problem, as it is slow, climbs badly and turns poorly, though its turrets can sometimes drive off a pursuing fighter. It came in Update 1.29.
do_217j_2: The J-2 succeeded the J-1 in 1942, adding FuG 202 Lichtenstein radar with its distinctive nose antennas and deleting the bomb bay; it achieved little and was relegated to training by mid-1944. In the game it is nearly identical to the J-1 in performance and armament, but the early radar helps locate targets in realistic and simulator battles. As with the J-1, the guns are what count, more than making up for its sluggishness. It arrived in Update 1.29.
do_217k_1: The K-1 gave the Do 217 a streamlined, fully glazed nose that cut drag and raised speed, switched the defensive guns to MG 81s, dropped the forward cannon and could carry a single SC 1800 internally; from September 1942 it flew night bombing and anti-shipping missions. In the game it is quick for a bomber, and the SC 1800, with 1,000 kg of TNT equivalent, gives it a big punch for close air support alongside SC 1000s and C250 incendiaries. F5W torpedoes need a drop speed below about 300 km/h, exposing it to ship fire, but a 700 km/h dive limit helps it escape fighters. It came in Update 1.29.
do_217m_1: With BMW 801s in short supply, the M-1 combined the K-series glazed nose with inline DB 603A engines, gaining about 80 km/h, and upgraded its defences with a forward MG 131 and twin rear MG 81s; it took part in Operation Steinbock and the sinking of the battleship Roma. In the game it is among the faster bombers it meets and can carry an SC 1800, SC 1000s, C250 incendiaries or F5W torpedoes, though the torpedoes demand a slow, vulnerable drop. Its high dive limit lets it outrun Spitfires and Yaks downhill. It came in Update 1.29.
do_217n_1: The N-1 was a Do 217 J night fighter fitted with DB 603A engines and a working bomb bay; about 240 entered service from April 1943, mainly against Soviet long-range bombers. In the game the new engines make it quicker than the J-2, and it brings radar, protected fuel tanks, a well-stocked forward battery and serviceable turrets. Single-engined fighters are another matter, as its handling is very poor and it climbs slowly. It came in Update 1.29.
do_217n_2: Derived from the DB 603-engined Do 217 M, the N series hunted Allied bombers at night, and the N-2 saved weight by deleting the bomb bay equipment and added four upward-firing MG 151 cannons behind the cockpit for attacks from below. Such Schräge Musik guns are rare in the game, and it pairs them with four forward MG 151s, four 7.92 mm machine guns and FuG 220 radar that detects targets at up to 8 km. Accurate bursts bring down fighters and bombers alike, but it handles like the bomber it is and is safest flying with friendly fighters. It arrived in Update 1.39.
do_335a_0: Claude Dornier's push-pull Do 335 Pfeil began as a 1942 fast bomber requirement, was reworked as a fighter-bomber and then pushed into the Emergency Fighter Programme, and only 37 were built; ten were pre-production A-0s, one of which survives at the National Air and Space Museum. In the game the A-0 leans towards interception: it has no bombs, but its 15 mm guns can be swapped for 20 mm. As on the A-1, handling and durability are mediocre, so speed and guns have to carry it, and its 30 mm cannon's AP belts let it attack tanks effectively. It arrived in Update 1.57 "Battle March".
do_335a_1: The A-1 was to be the first mass-produced Do 335, with uprated DB 603E-1 engines and bomb racks, but US forces captured the Oberpfaffenhofen factory in April 1945 and none of the 11 built saw service. It is a demanding aircraft: speed and guns are its only real assets, while the climb is mediocre, turning is poor, there is no armour and fires start easily. Ground attack is where it shines, with a reasonable bomb load and 30 mm AP belts that punch through tank roofs. It arrived in Update 1.57 "Battle March".
do_335b_2: Two Do 335s became B-2 "bomber destroyers" under the Emergency Fighter Programme, swapping their 15 mm guns for 20 mm MG 151/20s and gaining provision for two 300-litre drop tanks; little is recorded of their service, and neither survived the war. In the game its handling is too sluggish for dogfighting or escaping pursuit, so it works as an interceptor or attacker, using its great diving speed to strike first. Three 30 mm and two 20 mm cannons and up to 1,000 kg of bombs give it a heavy punch, and an exceptionally tough airframe means losing one engine mostly just slows it down. It arrived in Update 1.57 "Battle March".
douglas_a_1h: The A-1H, originally the AD-6, was the most-produced Skyraider at 712 aircraft and a vital US ground-support type in Vietnam, where in October 1965 Commander Clarence J. Stoddard marked the six-millionth pound of ordnance dropped by releasing a toilet in combat. It feels much like the earlier Skyraiders in the game, but carries a far larger load across many hardpoints, so it can be configured for whatever the battle needs. A "Special Weapon" option even lets players repeat Stoddard's stunt. It was a reward from Battle Pass Season IX, "Smell of Victory", in the "Fire and Ice" update.
douglas_ad_2: Ed Heinemann's Skyraider first flew as the XBT2D-1 in March 1945 and, though it missed the war, outlived the arrival of jets to serve in Korea and Vietnam, with 3,180 built across all versions; the AD-2 added a 2,700 hp Wright R-3350-26W, and 156 were made. In the game it pairs decent flight performance with a load of more than 4,000 lb, including bombs, rockets and torpedoes. Energy retention is poor, all the more so when loaded, but the far-forward cockpit offers a clear view and the air brake allows steep, steady dives onto targets. It came with Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory".
douglas_ad_4: The AD-4 added a second pair of 20 mm M3 cannons, better radar, a stronger undercarriage and G-suit provision to the Skyraider, and its 372 examples formed the core of US Navy and Marine strike forces in Korea. In the game it is a formidable ground attacker with a wide range of bombs and rockets, and its four cannons work well against both aircraft and ground targets. The price is weight: despite a powerful engine it sheds energy fast in manoeuvres, so a turning fight soon leaves it slow and easy for enemy fighters to pick off. It came with Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
douglas_ad_4_france: France bought 20 AD-4s, plus 88 AD-4N and 5 AD-4NA, in 1956 to replace its P-47s, using them in Algeria and other colonial conflicts until 1970, after which they passed to former colonies including Chad and Gabon. The French aircraft is identical to the American AD-4: a heavily armed attacker with many bomb and rocket options and four 20 mm cannons that are effective against air and ground targets alike. It is heavy, though, and turning bleeds its speed away quickly, leaving it vulnerable to fighters. It came with Update 1.73 "Vive la France".
douglas_ad_4na_france: The AD-4NA came from converting 100 AD-4N night attack aircraft back to standard AD-4 configuration during the Korean War, removing the night equipment and restoring the four 20 mm cannons; France bought five in 1956 and flew them in Algeria and the Chad–Libya border conflict until the 1970s. Apart from its appearance it performs exactly like the AD-4, pairing a broad choice of bombs and rockets with cannons useful against both aircraft and vehicles. Its weight remains the drawback, as it runs out of energy after a short turning fight. It arrived in Update 2.11 "Ground Breaking".
e7k2: Kawanishi's E7K2 was a three-seat reconnaissance seaplane developed in 1938 from the E7K1, with a stronger and more dependable Mitsubishi Zuisei 11 radial that improved its speed and performance; the Imperial Japanese Navy used it widely in the Pacific War until 1943. In the game ships can launch it for scouting; it was added in the "Winged Lions" update.
e8n2: The E8N2 was a catapult-launched Japanese reconnaissance seaplane carried aboard cruisers, seaplane tenders and capital ships in the Second Sino-Japanese and Pacific Wars, where it scouted, dive-bombed and spotted for naval gunfire; it improved on the E8N1 with a 630 hp Nakajima Kotobuki Kai 2 engine. In the game warships carry it as a scout plane; it was added in the "Winged Lions" update.
ef_2000_aesa: The German Tranche 4 Eurofighter brings Hensoldt's CAPTOR-E Mk 1 AESA radar and weapon system updates; the Luftwaffe ordered 30 single-seaters and 8 two-seaters in 2020 under the Quadriga programme, with deliveries expected from 2025. In the game it is close to the earlier EF-2000 but adds the CAPTOR-E, which detects and tracks more reliably than the mechanically scanned CAPTOR-M though without the full 100-degree gimbal of the British and Italian versions, and a PIRATE IRST that tracks aircraft without setting off their warning receivers. Missiles remain AIM-120B/C5 and AIM-9M, while SPICE 250 bombs join Brimstones and Paveways. It arrived in Update 2.53 "Line of Contact".
ef_2000_block_10: The Eurofighter Typhoon grew from a programme begun in 1983 that France left in 1985 to pursue the Rafale; Germany took it into service in 2003 to replace the F-4 Phantom, and deliveries came in tranches, with Tranche 2 adding better radar processing and far wider air-to-ground capability. The game's EF-2000 is a Tranche 2 aircraft. German Typhoons lack the PIRATE IRST, yet it remains an outstanding air-to-air fighter, with the thrust and agility to win close fights and the radar and missile count for long-range ones, while its enormous weapons load makes it just as dangerous to ground targets. It came with the "Storm Warning" update.
ef_2000_fgr4: The RAF's Typhoon entered service in 2003 to replace Phantoms and Jaguars; early Tranche 1 aircraft were designated F.2, and from Tranche 1 Block 5, which added the PIRATE IRST and basic ground-attack ability, all single-seat RAF Typhoons became FGR.4s. The game's version is a Tranche 2 aircraft: thanks to excellent performance and a large, mixed load, it fights well at any range and is formidable against ground targets. Its warning suite stands out: an RWR, a missile approach warner and, unusually even among Eurofighters, a laser warning system. It arrived in the "Storm Warning" update.
ef_2000_typhoon_aesa: The RAF's Tranche 3A Typhoon, first delivered in 2012, replaced the mechanically scanned radar with the CAPTOR-E Mk 0 AESA and improved avionics and electronic warfare equipment; Britain has since chosen the F-35 rather than ordering later tranches. In the game it keeps everything the FGR.4 offers and adds the CAPTOR-E, with excellent scanning and tracking and a 100-degree gimbal limit, plus fire-and-forget SPICE 250 bombs alongside Brimstones and Paveways. At short range, though, the AIM-120's limited agility remains a handicap. It arrived in Update 2.53 "Line of Contact".
ef_2000a: Italy's single-seat Eurofighter, designated F-2000A, entered Aeronautica Militare service in March 2004 in place of the F-104 after 41 years, and Italy was the first nation to declare initial operating capability, in December 2005. The game models a Tranche 2 Block 15 aircraft: its delta wing gives excellent agility, and it is able to supercruise after accelerating on afterburner. It carries AIM-120B, AIM-9L and AIM-9M missiles, plus Mk 83 and Mk 84 bombs, laser and inertially guided Paveway II, Paveway IV and GBU-54 bombs, up to 18 Brimstones and a LITENING III targeting pod. It came with the "Storm Warning" update.
ef_2000a_aesa: Italy ordered Tranche 3A Eurofighters with the CAPTOR-E Mk 0 AESA radar in 2014 and received the last in 2020; they are now its main multirole fighter. In the game the F-2000A (AESA) builds on the F-2000A with that radar, whose 100-degree gimbal, 200 km range and fast scan fix the weaknesses of the older CAPTOR-M and make AIM-120 shots more dependable. SPICE 250 bombs let it strike ground targets from a distance. Close-in shots remain awkward, as they are for all Eurofighters, because the AIM-120 is not very agile. It arrived in Update 2.53 "Line of Contact".
er-2_ach30b_early: The Yer-2 long-range bomber suffered from poor performance, accidents and fires, with 462 built between 1940 and 1945; in 1944 a version with ACh-30B diesels appeared, less prone to fire and strong enough for a third bomb rack raising the load to five tonnes and a ShVAK cannon in the upper turret, though poor build quality limited its impact. In the game its heavier load easily wipes out a base or two, and it has a ShVAK in place of the upper machine gun and a UBT in the nose. Flight performance and defences remain weak, so avoiding fighters is essential. It has been in the game since the open beta.
er-2_ach30b_late: The last production Yer-2 combined ACh-30B diesel engines, which used far less fuel but weighed more and needed a strengthened airframe, with a redesigned side-by-side cockpit, a dorsal 20 mm ShVAK and 12.7 mm UBTs in the nose and belly; production began in Irkutsk in December 1943 and it served until the Tu-4 replaced it. The wider cockpit distinguishes it from the early version in the game. It can carry three 1,000 kg and four 500 kg bombs, one more 1,000 kg bomb than earlier Yer-2s, and its dorsal cannon is a serious threat to attacking aircraft. It has been in the game since the open beta.
er-2_m105_mv3: Robert Bartini's Stal-7 airliner was turned into the Yer-2 long-range bomber under Vladimir Yermolaev after Bartini's 1938 arrest; it entered service in mid-1941, but delays to the intended M-106 engines left it with weaker M-105s, and early production aircraft had an MV-3 turret with a ShKAS instead of the planned heavy Berezin mount. In the game its large bomb load can level one or two bases, but very poor flight performance and light, ShKAS-only defences mean it should keep well away from enemy fighters. It has been in the game since the open beta.
er-2_m105_tat: This Yer-2 has the TAT-BT upper mount with a Berezin heavy machine gun, intended from the start but fitted only once turret production was standardised, in place of the early MV-3 and its ShKAS; like other M-105 aircraft it was underpowered because the planned M-106 engines were delayed. In the game that heavier upper gun is its main difference from the early version. It still carries enough bombs to destroy a couple of bases, while sluggish flying and weak defences make staying clear of fighters vital. It has been in the game since the open beta, though new players could no longer research it after Update 1.37.
er-2_m105r_lu2b: Series-production Yer-2s used M-105R engines, developed specifically for bombers with a lower reduction gear ratio, and later gained the LU-MV-2B ventral mount with a 12.7 mm Berezin in place of the ShKAS to counter attacks from behind. In the game that heavier belly gun is the main difference from the Yer-2 (M-105), slightly improving its odds against fighters. Its big bomb load can still flatten one or two bases, but poor handling and modest defences mean enemy aircraft are best avoided. It has been in the game since the open beta.
er-2_m105r_tat: This Yer-2 combines the bomber-specific M-105R engines of series production with the TAT-BT upper mount carrying a Berezin heavy machine gun, the intended configuration that replaced the early MV-3 turret's ShKAS. The type began as Bartini's Stal-7 airliner, was reworked into a bomber under Yermolaev, and was dogged by accidents and engine fires. In the game it can knock out a base or two per sortie, while poor flight performance and limited defences mean fighters are best avoided. It has been in the game since the open beta, but research for new players ended in Update 1.37.
etndard_4m: Dassault and Breguet built the Etendard IVM for the French Navy, which put it into service in 1962; powered by a single SNECMA Atar 8, it flew from carriers with air-to-surface and anti-ship weapons until retirement in the early 2000s. In the game it is an all-rounder: its guided ground-attack weapons are excellent for its level, while missiles and DEFA 552 cannons, together with very good performance when unloaded, make it a capable dogfighter. Lessons learned here carry over to the Super Etendard that follows it in the tree. It arrived in Update 1.95 "Northern Wind".
f-100a_china: Taiwan's F-100As were upgraded with F-100D-style tails and avionics but kept the smaller, flapless wing and fewer hardpoints of the early Super Sabre; with major air battles over the strait at an end, they flew patrols and training until spares shortages and three crashes forced their withdrawal in 1984. In the game it feels lighter and rolls faster than the F-100D, though the missing flaps hurt low-speed turning. Bullpups and AIM-9E Sidewinders are available, but bombs are limited and there are no rockets, while four 20 mm M39A1 cannons hit hard. Kept fast, it does best with quick diving passes. It arrived in Update 1.97 "Viking Fury".
f-100d: The F-100D, known early on as the "45-Sabre" for its 45-degree wing sweep, was designed first as a ground attacker and only secondly as a fighter, and the Super Sabre was the first US fighter to exceed the speed of sound in level flight. It was among the game's first jets with guided air-to-air missiles. It can carry up to 6,000 lb of bombs, Bullpups and Mighty Mouse rockets, or hunt aircraft with four 20 mm cannons and AIM-9B/E Sidewinders, using speed for diving attacks. Lacking countermeasures, it is vulnerable to faster or missile-armed opponents, but well flown it is strong in both roles. It arrived in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
