f-100d_france: France was the first air force outside the US to receive the F-100, from 1958, taking 85 F-100Ds and 15 F-100Fs; they flew combat missions against targets in Algeria, and the last unit, based in Djibouti, kept them until 1978. In the game it looks like the American F-100D but is set up for ground attack and downgraded for export, so it lacks most air-to-air avionics, the AIM-9E and the Bullpup. In exchange it can carry heavy Zuni rockets, an option never cleared on the American F-100D. It is at its best supporting ground forces in mixed battles, with boom-and-zoom tactics in the air. It came with Update 1.93 "Shark Attack".
f-104a: The F-104A was the first production Starfighter, with about 170 in USAF service; intended to replace the F-100, it fell short of requirements, was grounded over problems with its J79-GE-3A engine, and was judged weak as an interceptor for lacking all-weather capability and endurance, so many went abroad. In the game its J79, cannon and two AIM-9Bs make it formidable against largely subsonic opposition like the F-86 and Yak-38. It turns poorly, so it should stay fast and make diving passes rather than dogfight, and the situational AIM-9B is best for forcing opponents to turn or catching slow targets. It arrived in the "Starfighters" update.
f-104a_china: With PLA MiG-19s appearing in the 1960s, Taiwan asked for supersonic fighters, and under Project Alishan the US supplied 22 F-104As and 5 F-104Bs by 1960; they replaced F-86Fs at Taichung but went back to the US after six years and on to Jordan and Pakistan. In the game it matches the American F-104A and flies nothing like the F-100A before it: excellent speed, acceleration and climb, but very poor low-speed turning. The two AIM-9Bs disappoint, while the M61 Vulcan kills quickly, so disciplined boom-and-zoom is the way to fly it. It arrived in the "Starfighters" update.
f-104c: Tactical Air Command ordered almost 80 F-104Cs as ground-attack Starfighters, adding bomb carriage, an in-flight refuelling probe and better fire control; first flown in 1958, they served in Vietnam until the F-4D replaced them. In the game it differs from the F-104A mainly in carrying 750 lb bombs, Mighty Mouse rockets and BLU-1 incendiaries, alongside two AIM-9Bs and an improved M61A1 cannon. It is dangerous among its usual opponents, but with no flares and only early missiles it struggles badly against higher-ranked aircraft. It arrived in the "Starfighters" update.
f-104g: Over 1,000 F-104Gs were built by several manufacturers, making it the most common Starfighter, and Germany bought more than 900; a high accident rate, with over 250 aircraft and more than 100 pilots lost, earned it the name "Widowmaker" until the problems were addressed. In the game it is very fast but handles poorly, so it relies on speed and slashing passes rather than dogfights. Four AIM-9Js, countermeasures and an M61A1 with 750 rounds (only 7.5 seconds of firing) make it a capable fighter, and CCIP for guns, rockets and bombs makes it useful for ground attack too. It arrived in the "Starfighters" update.
f-104g_belgium: Belgium flew around 100 F-104Gs from 1963 to 1983, nearly all built locally by SABCA, which also produced some for Germany; they were the country's main fighter until the F-16A replaced them, after which most went into storage and some were sold to Turkey and Taiwan. The game's aircraft is FX-99, the last Belgian F-104G flying at retirement, now privately owned and restored to flying condition. It sits in the French tree and arrived in the "Seek & Destroy" update.
f-104g_china: Taiwan received F-104Gs from 1963 under Project Alishan, first from Lockheed and Canadair and later from German and Danish stocks; it was the only ROCAF Starfighter to fight PLA aircraft, in 1967, and some were converted for reconnaissance before the F-CK-1, Mirage 2000-5 and F-16 replaced them. In the game it is a clear step up from the ROCAF F-104A, with a stronger engine and a wider range of ordnance. Unlike the original German-export F-104G it can carry AIM-9J Sidewinders and AGM-12B Bullpups, which puts it near the top of the Starfighter family. It arrived in the "Starfighters" update.
f-104g_italy: Italy's first F-104G, a Lockheed-built aircraft, arrived on 3 March 1961 and was taken apart to prepare licence production; 105 were then built in Italy, serving mainly as AIM-9B-armed interceptors and sometimes as fighter-bombers, and leading to the Aeritalia F-104S. In the game its acceleration lets it climb quickly or run opponents down, and its 20 mm cannon and AIM-9Js are best used in fast diving attacks; turning fights, given its poor agility, rarely end well. Chaff and flares help it defeat infrared and semi-active radar missiles. It arrived in the "Direct Hit" update.
f-104j: The F-104J, nicknamed "Eiko" (Glory), was an F-104G stripped of ground-attack equipment, chosen in 1959 as the JASDF's interceptor against Soviet bombers and built by Mitsubishi; it was phased out after 1986 as F-4EJs and F-15Js arrived, with some passed to Taiwan and others turned into target drones. In the game it is a dedicated interceptor without precision strike capability. Slow-speed turning is poor, but its top speed and missile load make it a real danger to aircraft, especially attackers and bombers trying to reach their targets. It arrived in the "Starfighters" update.
f-104s: The F-104S developed the F-104G with Sparrow capability, the NASARR R-21G/H radar, more hardpoints and airframe changes; Fiat built over 200 from 1968 to 1979, around 40 went to Turkey, and it closed out Starfighter production. Recognisable by extra ventral fins, it is the fastest F-104 in the game and the one with the biggest payload. It can serve as a fast ground attacker with plenty of bombs and rockets or as an interceptor, and unusually for a Starfighter it can carry two AIM-7E Sparrows, though fitting them means removing the M61 Vulcan. It arrived in the "Starfighters" update.
f-104s_asa: The F-104S.ASA is an Italian member of the Starfighter family, identified from outside mainly by its extra ventral fins. Its standout feature is two Selenia Aspide missiles with semi-active radar homing, which no other Starfighter carries. It also has the highest speed and payload of the F-104 line, so it can switch between interception and fast ground attack with a large load of bombs and rockets. It arrived in the "Wind of Change" update.
f-104s_cb: Fiat delivered 40 new-build F-104S interceptors to Turkey in 1974–75, adding to an air force that already had two F-4E squadrons. Poor manoeuvrability makes it hard work in the game, yet its acceleration, climb and ballistic computer let it double as a fighter and a ground-attack aircraft: AIM-9P and AIM-7E missiles for aircraft and helicopters, bombs and rockets for supporting ground forces, and chaff and flares for protection. Unlike the tech-tree F-104S, it carries its 20 mm rotary cannon under the fuselage rather than in the nose. It arrived in the "Apex Predators" update.
f-105d: Republic's F-105D Thunderchief was the final production version of the single-seat fighter-bomber, turning it into an all-weather strike aircraft able to carry Bullpups and Sidewinders; 610 were built and it was one of the USAF's main fighter-bombers over Vietnam, hitting bases, bridges and supply lines. In the game it is a fast striker: bombs and guided missiles go onto bases or other targets, and its engine then carries it out of trouble quickly. AIM-9E Sidewinders let it take on aircraft too, but it cannot turn with conventional fighters, so long dogfights are a losing game. It arrived in the "Winged Lions" update.
f-4c: The F-4C was the US Air Force's first production Phantom II, a two-seat fighter-bomber that grew out of a development of the F3H Demon; the first production aircraft passed Mach 2 on its maiden flight in May 1963, and it served until 1989, most famously in Vietnam. In the game it relies on straight-line performance, accelerating hard and reaching high speeds, rather than on turning, and it can be loaded for air combat or ground attack. Its serious flaw is the lack of any countermeasures, leaving it exposed to missiles. It arrived in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
f-4e: Vietnam showed that fighters still needed guns, and podded Vulcans proved inaccurate, so McDonnell Douglas built the F-4E with an internal cannon; the YF-4E first flew in August 1965 and, with 1,370 built, it became the most produced Phantom. Agility is not its strength in the game, but acceleration and top speed are, and it can be fitted for almost any air or ground task. The older radar lacks a pulse-Doppler mode, which makes its AIM-7E-2 Sparrows harder to use well. It arrived in Update 1.97 "Viking Fury".
f-4e_iaf: Israel's F-4E Phantoms, called Kurnass ("Heavy Hammer"), went into action soon after delivery in the War of Attrition with Egypt and remained the main front-line fighter until F-15s and F-16s pushed them into ground attack; many were later upgraded to Kurnass 2000 standard. In the game it is close to the American F-4E but carries AIM-9D/G Sidewinders and cannot use GBU-15 bombs, while still offering many bombs and AGM-65B Mavericks. The long-burning AIM-9G suits long-range launches at high speed, the AIM-7E-2 is best fired from 3–6 km, and the lack of pulse-Doppler radar limits long-range engagements. It arrived in the "Winged Lions" update.
f-4e_kurnass_2000: The Kurnass 2000 upgraded Israel's F-4Es with the AN/APG-76 radar, an ASX-1 TISEO system for Popeye missiles, improved avionics and AIM-9L and Python 3 missiles. In the game it flies like a standard F-4E but has much stronger air-to-air weapons in all-aspect AIM-9Ls and Python 3s, plus AGM-65D Mavericks and Paveway II bombs with a Pave Spike pod. An EEGS gunsight helps with gun kills, the radar is powerful though there are no radar missiles, and it carries 290 countermeasures. Only the old airframe holds it back against MiG-29s and F-16As. It arrived in the "Sky Guardians" update.
f-4ej: Japan's F-4EJ was based on the USAF F-4E but without aerial refuelling or ground-attack capability; 140 were bought from 1968 and Mitsubishi built 138 under licence, serving as Japan's main air defence fighter until the last retired in December 2020. It is a versatile strike fighter in the game, able to take bombs, rockets, missiles and up to three additional gun pods, the last at some cost in speed and agility. Lacking the Agile Eagle modifications of the F-4E and F-4F, it turns worse than they do, so slashing attacks suit it better than turning with lighter jets. It came with Update 1.97 "Viking Fury".
f-4ej_adtw: This F-4EJ represents the Air Development and Test Wing, the JASDF's test unit and the first and last Japanese operator of the type until its retirement in 2021. It is identical to the tech-tree F-4EJ, carrying a wide range of air-to-air missiles, bombs, rockets and extra JM61 gun pods on top of a large internal ammunition supply. A weak radar undermines its four AIM-7s, and the AIM-9P is the best it has for close combat. It arrived in the "Apex Predators" update.
f-4ej_kai: Begun in 1980 to keep Japan's F-4EJs relevant, the Kai programme added new radar, fire control and modern missiles and bombing systems; 90 aircraft were converted, the first flying in 1984, and they served until 2021. In the game it shares the pulse-Doppler radar, RWR and weapons of the F-16A. AIM-7Fs suit long-range and head-on shots and AIM-9Ls quick kills up close, but it should not linger in turning fights with more agile jets. A riskier trick is to bleed speed with tight turns and air brakes, flare any missiles and let a pursuer overshoot, then finish it with an AIM-9 or the computed gunsight. It arrived in the "Direct Hit" update.
f-4f: Built only for the Luftwaffe, the F-4F Early was a cheaper, lighter F-4E: Sparrow capability, the rearmost fuel tank and other equipment were removed, saving about 1,500 kg, and deliveries began in late 1973. In the game it improves on the F-4C with an internal gun and AIM-9J Sidewinders, but like the real aircraft it cannot use guided weapons such as Bullpups or Mavericks. It was a reward from the Future Technology event in the "Ixwa Strike" update.
f-4f_kws_lv: With the Eurofighter years away, Germany modernised its F-4Fs from 1986 under the KWS programme, converting 110 to the air-defence LV standard with an AN/APG-65G radar, an updated rear cockpit, AIM-120 AMRAAM capability and a reshaped nose; they were the Luftwaffe's main fighter until the Typhoon arrived, and the last retired in 2014. In the game it is still the familiar Phantom, neither fast nor agile by the standards of its opponents. What keeps it competitive is the APG-65 radar paired with fire-and-forget AIM-120 AMRAAMs. It came with the "Seek & Destroy" update.
f-4f_late: Germany's F-4Fs began as stripped-down F-4Es without guided weapons, and between 1980 and 1983 they were retrofitted to use them again. Speed, countermeasures and AIM-9J Sidewinders make it a capable fighter in the game, and the M61 Vulcan's rate of fire and muzzle velocity finish targets quickly. Against ground targets it is just as useful, combining Mavericks with CCIP for its gun, bombs and rockets. It arrived in the "Red Skies" update.
f-4j: The F-4J was the US Navy and Marine Corps' development of the F-4B, with a strengthened airframe for carrier work, better take-off and landing performance and the AN/APG-59 radar with a Doppler mode; built from 1966 to 1972, it flew in Rolling Thunder and Linebacker before the F-14 replaced it. Long-range combat is its forte in the game, thanks to pulse-Doppler radar paired with AIM-7F Sparrows. It has no guided air-to-ground weapons, and without leading-edge slats it is less agile than the Air Force F-4E. It arrived in the "Winged Lions" update.
f-4jk: After the Falklands War the RAF needed a stopgap for mainland air defence until the Tornado F.3 arrived, and bought 15 refurbished ex-US Navy F-4Js that kept their J79 engines but were wired for Skyflash missiles; known as the F-4J(UK) or Phantom F.3, they served with No. 74 Squadron from 1984 to 1991. In the game it plays much like the American F-4J, but carries Skyflash instead of AIM-7F and has no helmet-mounted display, making target acquisition harder. It still competes well if flown low and fast, exploiting its acceleration and energy retention. It arrived in the "Apex Predators" update.
f-4k: To replace its Sea Vixens, the Fleet Air Arm bought the F-4K, or Phantom FG.1, a modified F-4J with a hinged nose radome, a longer nose gear leg for smaller British carriers and Rolls-Royce Spey turbofans; 48 were delivered from 1968, but the Spey's heat damaged flight decks, so only HMS Ark Royal operated them, until 1978. In the game it resembles the FGR.2, with AIM-9Gs, Skyflash, pulse-Doppler radar and Spey engines. Good acceleration and high-speed handling make it a strong air superiority fighter, and the 20 mm gun pod can be fitted or left off for better performance. It came with the "Starfighters" update.
f-4m_fgr2: The Phantom FGR.2 (F-4M) is the RAF's Phantom, rebuilt around Rolls-Royce Spey turbofans that gave more thrust than the American J79 but needed a wider fuselage, larger intakes and a redesigned rear end; it is recognisable by its squared-off tail and the absence of the F-4J's under-nose probe. Down low, the Speys give it noticeably better acceleration and climb than American Phantoms, getting it off the runway and up to altitude faster, but higher up the bulkier fuselage and engine characteristics let the F-4J pull ahead, and its top speed is lower. It arrived in Update 1.93 "Shark Attack".
f-4s: The F-4S was the US Navy's post-Vietnam upgrade of the F-4J, improving avionics, weapons, airframe and undercarriage, most notably with leading-edge slats and smokeless engines; it served until the Phantom left the Navy in the late 1980s. Flown much like the F-4J, it benefits from the slats in a turning fight, enough to surprise even some newer fighters, while at longer range its radar and Sparrows catch opponents who fail to defend in time. It arrived in the "Sky Guardians" update.
f-5a: Northrop conceived the N-156 in the mid-1950s as a cheap, easy-to-maintain supersonic fighter, and after the US services showed no interest it was chosen in 1962 for the Military Assistance Program, becoming the F-5A and one of the most successful export fighters. Its guns are the main weapon in the game, downing enemies with short bursts, since only two AIM-9Es can be carried; a small, light airframe makes it a superb dogfighter, and 60 countermeasures matter a lot at its level. Bombs and rockets are plentiful, but it is most effective hunting aircraft. It was a reward from the 2021 Export Order event in the "Direct Hit" update.
f-5a_china: The F-5A was the first of Northrop's long-lived F-5 lightweight fighter family, developed from the N-156; Taiwan's air force remains the largest operator of the family today with the F-5E/F. In the game its many loadouts make it highly versatile. With little more than two AIM-9Ps under the wings it turns and fights well against bigger, heavier jets, and loaded for ground attack it carries more bombs and rockets than its size suggests. It completes Taiwan's fighter line in the Chinese tree and arrived in the "Ixwa Strike" update.
f-5a_thailand: Thailand received F-5As from 1968 under an agreement allowing the USAF to operate from Thai bases during the Vietnam War, and gained more when South Vietnamese pilots fled with their aircraft in 1975; the F-5A/B were retired by the 1990s in favour of the F-5E/F. Part of the Thai sub-tree, it is identical to the American F-5A. Two AIM-9Es are its only missiles, but it is small and nimble enough to win dogfights on agility, and its wide range of ground weapons makes it a useful close air support aircraft. It arrived in the "Storm Warning" update.
f-5ag_norway: Norway replaced its F-86 Sabres with 56 F-5A(G)s and eight F-5B(G)s ordered in 1964, modified with Bullpup capability, an arrester hook and rocket-booster mounts; later upgrades added a Ferranti ballistic computer, RWR, countermeasures and, on seven aircraft, F-16-style HUDs, and the last were retired in 2007 after serving as Penguin missile testbeds. In the game it is fairly slow but agile and holds energy well at high speed. Compared with the American F-5A it gains AIM-9L Sidewinders, a better RWR and Penguin anti-ship missiles. It was a reward from the 2025 "Freedom Fighter" event in the Swedish tree.
f-5c: Twelve F-5As were evaluated by the USAF in Vietnam under the "Skoshi Tiger" programme and, fitted with refuelling probes, a lead-computing gunsight and extra belly armour, became F-5Cs, though the Pentagon declined to buy more. Excellent flight performance and two 20 mm nose cannons do most of the work in the game, as the pair of AIM-9Es cannot be relied on. Countermeasures, valuable at its level, and a low heat signature help it shake off infrared missiles, and while it can carry bombs it is far better used as a fighter. This premium arrived in the "Red Skies" update.
f-5e: The F-5E Tiger II improved the F-5A/B with a better wing, more powerful engines and modern avionics, drawing on Vietnam experience; it entered US service in the 1970s, served for over 30 years and is still flown by countries such as Taiwan, South Korea and Brazil. In the game excellent handling suits it to both dogfighting and ground support, and its stores include rockets, gun pods, AGM-65B Mavericks, air-to-air missiles and both HE and incendiary bombs. Beginners pick it up quickly, and experienced pilots make it very dangerous. It arrived in the "Red Skies" update.
f-5e_aidc: Taiwan began assembling F-5E/Fs locally with AIDC under Project Peace Tiger in 1973 to replace its F-86F and F-100 fleets after plans for the F-4 fell through; six batches were built, and they formed the core of the air force until two fatal accidents in the 2020s hastened their retirement. In the game it matches the American F-5E, including its missiles and a range of stores from rocket pods to 2,000 lb bombs. The J-7E is the better dogfighter in the Chinese tree, but no other aircraft there offers four AGM-65 Mavericks for precise attacks from a distance. It arrived in the "Danger Zone" update.
f-5e_fcu_thailand: South Vietnam received more than 150 F-5s, and many were flown to Thailand after the fall of Saigon; the older models soon retired, but the F-5Es have been upgraded repeatedly and remain in Royal Thai Air Force service. In the game the F-5E FCU keeps the F-5E's light weight, agility and excellent energy retention, and fixes the family's main weakness by carrying four all-aspect missiles where its relatives manage two rear-aspect ones. A generous choice of ground weapons makes it strong in close air support as well, and it is forgiving enough for less experienced pilots. It arrived in the "Alpha Strike" update as part of the Japanese tree.
f-5e_switzerland: Switzerland bought 98 F-5E Tiger IIs in 1981, after trials in the late 1970s, as a low-cost aircraft suited to its new air-superiority doctrine and its airfields, replacing ageing Hunters in that role; despite repeated attempts to retire it, it served for 43 years until 2024. In the German tree it is identical to the American F-5E. Its agility suits both dogfights and ground support, and its options range from air-to-air missiles, bombs and gun pods to rockets and AGM-65B Mavericks. It is approachable for newcomers yet effective in skilled hands. It arrived in Update 2.47 "Leviathans".
f-5t_thailand: The F-5T Tigris was Thailand's second F-5E upgrade, designed with Israel's Elbit in the late 1990s: a new radar and rudder, digital multifunction displays, fresh cockpit glazing and a helmet-mounted sight, applied to 18 aircraft from 2002 before a further upgrade created the F-5TH. In the game it builds on the F-5E FCU with new weapons. It gives up the option of carrying extra all-aspect missiles in exchange for two AIM-9Ls, which outperform the FCU's AIM-9P-4s, and a helmet-mounted display makes aiming easier. It arrived in the "Storm Warning" update as part of the Thai sub-tree.
f-5th_thailand: Budget limits kept Thailand's F-5Ts flying, so from 2015 Elbit and Thai firm RV Connext produced the F-5TH Super Tigris, swapping one 20 mm gun for an EL/M-2032 radar, adding the Link-T/TH datalink and a LITENING III pod, and clearing it for AIM-9M, Python 4 and Derby missiles. In the game the lost gun buys a much wider arsenal, including infrared and active radar missiles such as a pair of beyond-visual-range Derbys, more guided ground weapons and a helmet display with thermal and night vision. Against fourth-generation fighters, however, its modest speed and acceleration leave it struggling in dogfights. It arrived in the "Tusk Force" update.
f-80: The P-80C, redesignated F-80C in 1948, was the last production Shooting Star; later batches received the J33-A-35 with 15% more thrust, and fast-firing M3 Brownings were fitted. F-80Cs flew most US Shooting Star missions in Korea and left Guard and Reserve service in 1958. Compared with the F-80A, the new engine and six faster-firing, longer-ranged M3s make it a much better fighter, and it can lift up to four 1,000 lb bombs. Its water injection gives roughly 100 seconds of extra power, most valuable when accelerating from low speed. It came in Update 1.33.
f-80a: The F-80 Shooting Star was the first American jet fighter to enter service; designed in only 143 days, it suffered serious problems that killed several test pilots, including top ace Richard Bong, arrived too late for the Second World War and became the first US jet to fight in Korea. In the game it is a training ground for jet flying: speed must never be given away except to zoom-climb, especially when facing stronger opponents. Its nose-mounted M2 Brownings fire slowly for high-speed fights but are accurate in head-ons and set piston aircraft alight quickly, and it can carry HVARs and 1,000 lb bombs. It arrived in Update 1.39.
f-82e: The Twin Mustang joined two P-51H fuselages to give long-range missions a second pilot; the USAAF ordered prototypes in 1944, and around 96 F-82Es were delivered with Allison V-1710 engines after concerns over Merlin supply and cost. In the game it is very fast, with a 742 km/h top speed and an 854 km/h structural limit. Six M3 Brownings in the centre section can be supplemented by a pod with eight more M2s, which adds drag in air combat but gives plenty of ammunition for ground attack, alongside bombs and rockets. It arrived in Update 1.39.
f-84b: Republic's first jet, the F-84 Thunderjet, entered service in B form, essentially the YP-84A with faster-firing M3 Brownings, but unresolved problems limited the F-84B and C to about four years of service. In the game its weak engine means a long take-off and slow climb, though it is fast in level flight and dives once at altitude; exceeding Mach 0.8 risks structural failure, which hurts against faster MiG-15s. It is a stable gun platform with six M3s (300 rounds each) and carries bombs up to 1,000 lb, HVARs and Tiny Tims. Loaded, it should avoid dogfights; once empty, speed and boom-and-zoom keep it alive. It arrived in Update 1.39.
f-84f: The swept-wing F-84F Thunderstreak began in 1949 as a faster development of the Thunderjet and switched to the J65, a licence-built Sapphire, to improve climb and high-altitude performance; over 2,000 were delivered by 1957. Pilots liked its robustness, though it needed a high landing speed, and it served with the Air National Guard until the early 1970s. Acceleration is its weak point in the game, worse still under a bomb load, which is why a lighter fuel load helps. The six 12.7 mm guns deal with ground targets but feel weak against aircraft, making air combat frustrating. It arrived in the "Hot Tracks" update.
f-84f_france: France, lacking a dedicated strike jet while the Vautour II was still in development, bought 328 F-84Fs and 88 RF-84Fs from the US, receiving the first in 1955. In the game its strengths are a big load, good top speed and easy-to-aim guns, with CCRP for bombing and CCIP for the guns. Starting on the ground and accelerating poorly, a bomb-laden F-84F often reaches its targets late; in air combat it wants height and a speed above roughly Mach 0.8. It arrived in the "Hot Tracks" update.
f-84f_germany: More than 400 F-84Fs went to West Germany's re-formed Luftwaffe between the late 1950s and early 1960s, starting with JaBoG 31, but losses exceeded 25%, and the F-104 that replaced it from 1966 continued the pattern. In the game its payload runs from 250 lb to 2,000 lb bombs plus rockets, and the centre-mounted M3s shred soft targets such as pillboxes, anti-aircraft guns and artillery. Air combat is another matter: many aircraft it meets fly better, leaving it ill-equipped to defend itself. It arrived in the "Hot Tracks" update.
f-84f_iaf: During the 1956 Suez Crisis, French F-84Fs flew with Israeli markings to conceal France's involvement, bombing Egyptian targets in Sinai from bases in North Africa. In the game it is identical to other F-84Fs, diving onto targets or reaching bombing points before enemies can respond, and its premium bonuses make it a good earner in the bombing role. It arrived in the "Hot Tracks" update but was removed from the French tree with "Winged Lions" and can no longer be obtained, as a copy is now sold in the Israeli tree.
f-84f_israel_iaf: The first F-84s to fly under Israeli command were three French squadrons sent for the 1956 Suez campaign and painted in Israeli colours to hide France's role. It is no standout in performance, avionics or firepower, but it can do many jobs: its CCRP sight places bombs accurately on bases and static targets, and once lightened it handles respectably, with six heavy machine guns that punish head-on passes. It arrived in the "Wind of Change" update.
f-84f_italy: Italy's 102nd Group received the first F-84Fs in 1956, replacing F-84Gs, followed by the 101st and 103rd; pilots disliked its handling, yet it flew with the Diavoli Rossi aerobatic team in 1958–59, and its last task was escorting Pope Paul VI to Israel in January 1964 before the G.91 and F-104G took over. In the game its swept wings help it build speed but it bleeds energy in manoeuvres, so it suits energy and boom-and-zoom tactics. A good choice of bombs and rockets makes it useful for ground support or bombing. It arrived in the "Hot Tracks" update.
f-84g: The F-84G was Republic's refined Thunderjet, with a stronger engine and structure, secure wingtip tanks, better avionics and radar, in-flight refuelling and Mark 7 nuclear capability; it served the US into the mid-1960s and Greece until 1991. Nicknamed the "Lead Sled", it needs a take-off run of about 1,500 m in the game but is very stable once airborne. Six M3 Brownings (300 rounds each) and loads of bombs up to 1,000 lb, HVARs and Tiny Tims make it a capable fighter-bomber, though it should stay fast and avoid dogfights until its ordnance is gone. It arrived in Update 1.77 "Advancing Storm".
f-84g-31-re_china: The F-84G-31-RE was the last straight-wing F-84 production block and served Taiwan's air force as a stopgap for seven years, scoring victories over MiGs once thought out of its reach. In the game it closely resembles the earlier ROCAF F-84G, differing mainly in block number. Its modest engine limits it as a fighter, but its ground-attack weapons fill an important gap in the Chinese tree, and as a premium it lets players practise jet ground attack without ballistic computers with the usual premium bonus to research points and silver lions. It arrived in the "Sky Guardians" update.
f-84g_china: Taiwan's air force received the Thunderjet as one of its first American jets. In the game it is often the first jet Chinese players fly and eases the move from piston aircraft. It shares much with Republic's P-47 in the same tree: a big but clean airframe, six .50 calibre guns and heavy loads of bombs and rockets, here with jet speed. More forgiving than the PLA's MiG-9, it holds its own both in the air and in ground battles. It arrived in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
f-84g_france: France bought 140 F-84Es and F-84Gs in the mid-1950s, needing a modern close air support aircraft for conflicts across its overseas territories; the G was the most developed straight-wing Thunderjet, with a stronger engine and structure, in-flight refuelling and nuclear capability. In the game it lives on its speed and becomes an easy target when slow. It is not the fastest at its level, but its six centre-line M3s can bring down fighters, and with two 1,000 lb bombs or Tiny Tims and HVARs aboard it should keep out of dogfights until the load is dropped. It arrived in Update 1.79 "Project X".
f-84g_greece: Greece received 200 F-84G Thunderjets between 1952 and 1955 after joining NATO, its air force's first jet fighters, and flew them until Canadair Sabres replaced them in 1960. In the Israeli tree it is identical to the American F-84G. Like other early jets it depends on speed, so choosing the moment to commit to a fight, and to leave it, matters more than turning ability. It can also carry a variety of heavy loads for ground support. It arrived in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey".
f-84g_italy: Italy's 5th Stormo received F-84Gs at Villafranca from April 1952, with coloured lightning markings identifying each group, and its aerobatic team "Guizzo", known as the Thundering Jets, toured Europe for three years and inspired a film. In the game it ranks among the better early jets. Its six M3 Brownings fire fast enough to down aircraft quickly, HVARs and bombs suit close air support, and it flies well at speed, though letting the speed drop leaves it sluggish. It arrived with the Italian air tree in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica".
f-84g_thailand: Thailand received 31 F-84Gs in 1956 under a pact that let the US build U-Tapao air base; they were the country's first jets and flew in the Vietnam War and Laotian Civil War until retirement in 1966. In the Japanese tree it is identical to the American F-84G. Speed is both its defence and its weapon, and a slow Thunderjet is an easy kill, so it should strike and extend rather than turn. It can also carry a range of heavy ordnance for ground support. It arrived in the "Storm Warning" update.
f-86_canadair_german: Canada licence-built the F-86 as the Canadair Sabre, gradually diverging from the American design; the Mk 5 had the Orenda 10 engine, a new wing and other changes giving performance close to the F-86F-30, and Germany received 75 ex-RCAF Mk 5s as a stopgap before its Mk 6 order, most being scrapped in 1962. In the game the Orenda's roughly 2,800 kgf, about 8% more than the F-86F-40's J47, gives it noticeably better acceleration and climb. Otherwise it keeps six nose-mounted M3 machine guns and the F-86F-30's HVARs and 750 lb and 1,000 lb bombs. It arrived in Update 1.39.
f-86_cl_13_mk4_italy: The Canadair Sabre Mk.4 was meant to receive the Orenda 10 but kept the J47-GE-13 because the Canadian engine was not ready, making it largely a Mk.2 with minor changes; Italy took over 170 from the RAF and flew them until the F-104 arrived. In the game it handles much like the F-86A-5, with the same guns and similar acceleration, though its all-flying tail improves manoeuvring. Most opponents climb and accelerate better, and the M3s tend to damage jets rather than destroy them outright, so it is a decent but limited fighter. It arrived in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
f-86_cl_13b_mk6: The Mk 6 was the last Canadair Sabre, powered by the Orenda 14 with 14% more thrust for better climb, speed and ceiling; Germany bought over 200, including the very last one built. In the game it is one of the best Sabres, with leading-edge slats and low weight giving excellent agility and the engine out-climbing and out-accelerating the F-86F. It keeps six M3 machine guns and adds AIM-9Bs, useful for forcing turns or catching slow targets. Without flares it is vulnerable to AIM-9Ls and R-60Ms, so all-aspect missile carriers such as the Su-25 and A-10 are best avoided. It arrived in Update 1.87 "Locked On".
